fix(huggingface): align tool message serialization with OpenAI API spec (#993)

* fix(huggingface): align tool message serialization with OpenAI API spec

The HuggingFace provider's custom Message types were not fully compliant
with the OpenAI Chat Completions API specification, causing 422 errors when
calling OpenAI-compatible endpoints (router.huggingface.co, Cerebras, and
other providers via custom base_url).

Three serialization issues fixed to match OpenAI API spec:

1. Tool role capitalization
   - Error: `messages[N].role: Input should be 'system', 'user', 'assistant' or 'tool'`
   - Received: "Tool" (capitalized)
   - Fixed: `#[serde(rename = "tool", alias = "Tool")]`
   - Serializes as lowercase "tool", accepts both for deserialization

2. Function arguments format
   - Error: `messages[N].tool_calls[N].function.arguments: Input should be a valid string`
   - Received: `{"cluster_id":"..."}` (JSON object)
   - Fixed: Use `json_utils::stringified_json` (consistent with OpenAI provider)
   - Serializes arguments as JSON string: `"{\"cluster_id\":\"...\"}"`

3. Tool content format
   - Error: `messages[N].content: Input should be a valid string`
   - Received: `["result"]` (JSON array, from OneOrMany<String> default serialization)
   - Fixed: Custom serializer joins array elements with newlines
   - `OneOrMany::one("result")` → `"result"`
   - `OneOrMany::many(["a", "b"])` → `"a\nb"`

OpenAI's function calling examples [1] and Cerebras documentation [2] confirm
these requirements. Tested with Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 via
HuggingFace/Cerebras. Multi-turn tool conversations now work correctly.

[1] https://github.com/openai/openai-cookbook/blob/main/examples/How_to_call_functions_with_chat_models.ipynb
[2] https://inference-docs.cerebras.ai/capabilities/tool-use

* fix: format code and restore backward-compatible deserialization

- Split long line in serialize_tool_content for proper formatting
- Restore backward-compatible arguments deserializer that accepts both
  stringified JSON and raw JSON objects during deserialization
- Maintains OpenAI API compliance by serializing as stringified JSON
- Fixes test_deserialize_message test failure

* refactor: use imported types instead of absolute paths

- Add Serializer to imports
- Use Value instead of serde_json::Value
- Use Deserializer instead of serde::Deserializer
- Use Serializer instead of serde::Serializer

Removes needless absolute references while maintaining correctness.

fix(streaming): use .instrument() instead of span.enter() to prevent span leak (#1108)

Using span.enter() inside async_stream::stream! holds the guard across
yield points, which causes thread-local span context to leak to other
concurrent tasks when they run on the same thread.

This fix replaces span.enter() with .instrument() from tracing_futures,
which properly propagates span context without polluting the thread-local
context.

References:
- https://docs.rs/tracing/latest/tracing/span/struct.Span.html#in-asynchronous-code
- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-clippy/issues/8722

Also includes a test to verify span context isolation works correctly.

fix: StreamingPromptHook panic when chat_history is empty (#1132)

The streaming implementation's `on_completion_call` hook was incorrectly
trying to get the prompt from `chat_history.last()` instead of using the
`current_prompt` variable.

This caused two bugs:
1. Panic when using `.with_hook()` without prior chat history (empty vec)
2. Wrong semantics - hook received last history message instead of actual prompt

The fix uses `current_prompt` directly, which aligns with the streaming
architecture where the prompt is kept separate from chat_history until
after the completion.

fix(streaming): disambiguate tool calls sharing the same index from API gateways (#1443)

Some API gateways (e.g. LiteLLM, OneAPI) do not follow the OpenAI
streaming convention of assigning each parallel tool call a unique
index. Instead, they emit multiple distinct tool calls all at index 0,
distinguishing them only by their `id` field. The previous accumulation
logic keyed solely on index, causing later tool calls to overwrite and
corrupt earlier ones into a single merged entry.

Detect this by comparing the incoming `id` against the existing entry
at the same index; when a new id appears, flush the old entry as a
completed tool call before starting a fresh accumulation.

Also:
- Extract shared MockStreamingClient into http_client::mock
- Remove unused final_tool_calls accumulator
- Fix inconsistent indentation in tool call delta handling

Signed-off-by: Jiawei Zhao <Phoenix500526@163.com>

reqwest 0.13 moved system proxy support behind a feature flag
(system-proxy), unlike 0.12 where it was always enabled. Without
this feature, reqwest ignores $http_proxy/$https_proxy environment
variables and attempts direct TCP connections, which fails in
environments that require a proxy for external access.

* fix(openai): add reasoning_content to StreamingDelta for OpenAI-compatible providers

The OpenAI Chat Completions streaming parser (StreamingDelta) does not
parse the easoning_content field from SSE chunks, causing reasoning/
thinking content from OpenAI-compatible providers to be silently dropped.

This affects all models that send easoning_content via the standard
Chat Completions streaming format, including:
- GLM-4.7 (Zhipu AI)
- DeepSeek models via OpenAI-compatible endpoints
- Qwen with thinking mode
- vLLM / Ollama OpenAI-compatible endpoints

The fix adds easoning_content: Option<String> to StreamingDelta and
yields RawStreamingChoice::ReasoningDelta events when present, matching
the existing pattern in the DeepSeek-specific provider.

Note: RawStreamingChoice::ReasoningDelta was already defined in
streaming.rs (added in PR #1395), but the generic OpenAI streaming
parser never utilized it.

fix: forward max_tokens in Chat Completions API requests (#1495)

The Chat Completions provider's `CompletionRequest` struct was missing
the `max_tokens` field. When users set `.max_tokens(N)` on the agent
builder, the value was accepted and stored in the core
`CompletionRequest` but silently discarded during conversion to the
OpenAI Chat Completions request — the `TryFrom` destructured with `..`
which dropped it, and the struct had no field to receive it.

The Responses API provider correctly handles this via
`max_output_tokens`, so only the Chat Completions path was affected.

The fix adds `max_tokens: Option<u64>` to the provider's
`CompletionRequest`, extracts it from the core request during
conversion, and includes it in the serialized API request.

fix(openai): strengthen streaming tool call dedup to prevent false evictions (#1510)

The deduplication heuristic added in v0.32 evicts a tool call entry when
a new chunk arrives at the same index with a different id.  This breaks
providers (e.g. GLM-4) that send a unique id on every SSE chunk for the
same logical tool call — each chunk triggers a false eviction, yielding
incomplete fragments.

Strengthen the condition to require both id AND name to differ before
evicting.  A genuinely new tool call at the same index (the
LiteLLM/OneAPI gateway case) always carries a new non-empty name,
while continuation chunks have an empty name.

Adds a regression test reproducing the GLM-4 scenario from issue #1508.

fix: embedding deserialization breaks with serde_json/arbitrary_precision (#1518)

* fix: embedding deserialization breaks with serde_json/arbitrary_precision

Change embedding response structs to use `Vec<serde_json::Number>`
instead of `Vec<f64>`, then convert to f64 after parsing.

When `serde_json/arbitrary_precision` is enabled (commonly pulled in
by `rust_decimal/serde-with-arbitrary-precision`), all JSON numbers
are represented as strings internally. This causes `Vec<f64>` fields
to fail deserialization with:
"data did not match any variant of untagged enum ApiResponse"

`serde_json::Number` deserializes correctly regardless of whether
`arbitrary_precision` is active, then `.as_f64()` converts to the
expected type.

Affects all providers: Gemini, OpenAI, Mistral, OpenRouter, Together,
and Cohere.

The Copilot API exposes an OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint
but omits several response fields that the standard OpenAI specification
requires (object, created, finish_reason). This provider derives from
the OpenAI module, reusing its request/message types while relaxing the
response contract with Option<T> + serde(default).

- CompletionResponse.object: Option<String> (omitted by Copilot API)
- CompletionResponse.created: Option<u64> (omitted by Copilot API)

Add Serialize/Deserialize derives to CompletionRequest, PromptResponse, TypedPromptResponse (#1637)

* Add Serialize/Deserialize derives to CompletionRequest, PromptResponse, TypedPromptResponse

All field types in `CompletionRequest`, `PromptResponse`, and `TypedPromptResponse<T>` already implement `Serialize` and `Deserialize`, but the structs themselves don't derive these traits. This prevents downstream code from serializing complete inference requests for debugging, replay, or persistence. Saving a fully-assembled `CompletionRequest` (with chat history, tools, preamble, etc.) to JSON for later replay is useful for reproducing inference behavior without running the full application stack.

Backward compatibility: adding trait implementations is non-breaking. No existing behavior or API changes.

fix(telemetry): emit OTel-standard gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens across providers (#1666)

* fix: emit OTel-standard cache_read.input_tokens across providers

Provider spans declared `gen_ai.usage.cached_tokens` (non-OTel) but the
shared telemetry helpers (`SpanCombinator::record_token_usage`,
`openai_chat_completions_compatible::record_usage`) write the OTel-
standard `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens`. Because `tracing`
silently drops `.record()` for fields not declared on the span, cached-
token values were being computed and thrown away on every provider whose
span did not declare the OTel name.

Declare `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens` on every affected span
across OpenAI, Azure, Cohere, Gemini (incl. interactions_api), Groq,
DeepSeek, HuggingFace, Mistral, OpenRouter, Together, xAI, Copilot,
and llamafile. Emit `cache_read.input_tokens` from the OpenAI chat-
completions compatible helper and the OpenAI Responses API record
sites. Do not emit `cache_creation.input_tokens` on OpenAI-family spans
— those APIs have no cache-creation concept and a hardcoded 0 would be
misleading rather than informative. Anthropic, which does report cache
creation, is unchanged.

Remove the non-OTel `gen_ai.usage.cached_tokens` attribute from every
path this change touches: drop the span declaration and, on paths whose
only recording sites are modified here, drop the record calls too. Only
the OTel-standard attribute is emitted from these paths.

Spans that record cache tokens entirely through their own inline
`span.record("gen_ai.usage.cached_tokens", ...)` calls (e.g. non-
streaming paths of Groq, DeepSeek, Copilot; standalone files like
Galadriel, Hyperbolic, Mira, Moonshot, Ollama, Perplexity, ChatGPT;
non-streaming Together and xAI) are out of scope for this change and
continue to emit only `cached_tokens`.

* fix: emit cache_read.input_tokens on 5 providers missed by prior commit

Galadriel, Hyperbolic, Mira, Moonshot, and Perplexity all route their
streaming paths through `send_compatible_streaming_request`, whose
shared `record_usage` helper was updated in the prior commit to write
the OTel-standard `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens`. These five
provider spans still declared `gen_ai.usage.cached_tokens`, so the
newly-recorded value was silently dropped by `tracing` — and since
none of these files inline-records `cached_tokens` either, their
streaming paths were emitting no cache-read metric at all after the
prior commit landed.

Rename the declaration to `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens` on
both the non-streaming and streaming span in each file, matching the
pattern the prior commit already applied across the other providers.
The non-streaming rename is a no-op (no recorder targets the field on
that path) but keeps both spans in each file consistent.

* fix: complete cache_read.input_tokens rename across remaining providers

Prior two commits partially renamed gen_ai.usage.cached_tokens to the
canonical OTel GenAI attribute gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens but
left several providers (and some streaming-vs-non-streaming paths within
a provider) emitting the old name. Finish the rename in chatgpt,
copilot, deepseek (non-streaming), groq (non-streaming), ollama,
together/completion, and xai/completion so every span consistently
emits cache_read.input_tokens.

- rig-memory: `MemoryPolicy::apply` stays the required method;
  `apply_with_demoted` becomes the optional companion with default

  `tracked_conversations` are infallible — a poisoned state lock is
  treated as nothing-to-forget / zero-tracked rather than a
  caller-visible error. `Result<(), MemoryError>` and
  `Result<usize, MemoryError>` were friction at every call site for
  what are diagnostic / cleanup helpers.
- rig-memory: fix `clear`-vs-in-flight-hook race. The post-hook tail
  no longer resurrects a watermark entry that a concurrent `clear`

  next load on a freshly-populated backend would otherwise skip a real

  `OneOrMany::first_ref` instead of `first` when checking for an
  orphan leading tool-result, avoiding a clone of potentially large
  `ToolResultContent` payloads on every truncation.
- rig-memory: `HeuristicTokenCounter` switches its sizing input from
  `str::chars().count()` (O(n) Unicode-scalar walk) to `str::len()`
  (O(1) UTF-8 byte length). The configurable ratio is renamed
  `chars_per_token` -> `bytes_per_token` to match. Bytes are a
  better-aligned proxy for byte-pair-encoding tokenizers and the
  resulting count is monotonic in input size; for ASCII the result is
  unchanged, for non-ASCII the counter slightly over-estimates which
  is the safe direction for a hard budget. Doc updated; the
  unreleased `heuristic_counter_clamps_invalid_chars_per_token` test
  is renamed to match.
- rig-memory: `DemotingPolicyMemory` watermark lookup uses a
  `HashMap::get_mut` fast path on `load` and only allocates a new
  `String` key when first recording state for a previously-unseen
  conversation that has demotion work; the prior code allocated a
  `String` on every load via `entry(to_string()).or_default()`.

  in-flight gate. A hook error is returned only to the caller that
  drove delivery; concurrent loads that short-circuited on
  `in_flight` see `Ok(kept)` even on hook failure, and the next

  `MemoryError` becoming `#[non_exhaustive]` plus the new

feat(memory): add Compactor trait, CompactingMemory adapter, and TemplateCompactor (#1748)

* feat(rig-core): add Compactor trait for evicted-message rollups

DemotionHook is a one-way drain that observes messages a memory policy
truncated out of active history. Compactor is the inverse: it returns a
single Message-shaped Artifact derived from the evicted prefix and an
optional carry_over (the previous summary), which a composing adapter
splices back into the loaded history. The resulting prompt shape is
[summary, ...recent_window] instead of a verbatim suffix.

The trait lives in rig_core::memory so any backend can implement it
without taking a rig-memory dependency. The composing CompactingMemory
adapter and a zero-dependency TemplateCompactor reference implementation
land in rig-memory.

Per-conversation watermarks are in-process only, so Compactor
implementations with durable side effects (LLM calls, vector-store
writes) must deduplicate per the same idempotency contract that already
applies to DemotionHook.

* feat(rig-memory): add CompactingMemory adapter and TemplateCompactor

Where DemotingPolicyMemory only observes messages a policy truncates,
CompactingMemory<M, P, C> substitutes them: it derives a single
Message-shaped Artifact from the evicted prefix (and the previous
summary, if any) via a Compactor, and splices that artifact at the
front of the loaded history. The resulting prompt shape is
[summary_message, ...kept_window], with the summary rolling forward on
every load that produces newly-evicted messages — the canonical
recursive-summary pattern for long-running agents.

Concurrency contract at the compaction seam: concurrent loads on the
same conversation_id are serialised by an in-flight gate. Only one load
at a time invokes the compactor; others observe the gate and return the
previously-stored summary spliced in front of kept, without re-running
the compactor. A clear that lands while compaction is in flight is not
overwritten by the post-await state update — covered by
compacting_concurrent_with_clear_does_not_resurrect_state.

Watermarks and the carry-over summary are in-process only. Compactor
implementations with durable side effects must deduplicate.

clear() drops the carry-over so a freshly-populated backend re-compacts
from scratch.

TemplateCompactor is a zero-dependency, no-LLM rollup useful as a
default and for tests. It produces a TextSummary that converts into a
Message::User containing a header + previous-summary + per-line
'role: text' body, with an optional with_max_bytes cap that truncates
deterministically.

* fix(memory): address PR #1748 review feedback

Three follow-ups against the Copilot bot review on
0xPlaygrounds/rig#1748, all on the same commit (5e7e3d7d).

1. RAII InFlightGuard for the compaction gate
   (crates/rig-memory/src/lib.rs)

   The previous code in CompactingMemory::load set in_flight = true
   before awaiting the compactor and only cleared it on the post-await
   success/error branches. If the load future was dropped while
   awaiting (caller timeout, tokio::select! cancellation) or if the
   compactor panicked, the flag stayed set permanently and every
   subsequent load on that conversation short-circuited on the gate
   without ever invoking the compactor again.

   The fix introduces a local InFlightGuard<'_, A> with a Drop impl
   that re-acquires the state lock and clears in_flight unless the
   guard was disarmed. The post-await branches still update absorbed
   and summary atomically and then disarm the guard so its Drop is a
   no-op on the happy path; abnormal exits (panic, cancellation, the
   "watermark exceeds slice" invariant break) drop the guard and
   release the gate. A missing entry is treated as a no-op so a
   concurrent clear+forget on the same conversation continues to
   correctly drop the state map entry rather than resurrecting it.

   Covered by compacting_dropped_load_releases_in_flight_gate, which
   spawns a load, aborts the JoinHandle while the compactor is parked
   on a Notify, and asserts that the next load is able to enter the
   compactor a second time. The pre-existing
   compacting_concurrent_with_clear_does_not_resurrect_state continues
   to pass because the guard's Drop only mutates an existing entry.

2. truncate_summary locates the body boundary in buf
   (crates/rig-memory/src/lib.rs)

   TemplateCompactor::with_header accepts arbitrary strings, but the
   previous truncate_summary computed the body start as
   header.len() + 1, implicitly assuming a single-line header. A
   header containing an embedded \n would mis-locate the body
   boundary and could drop or retain unexpected characters.

   truncate_summary now scans buf for the first \n and treats that
   as the header/body boundary, regardless of how the caller chose
   to format the header. The header argument is no longer needed and
   has been removed. Covered by
   template_compactor_caps_summary_with_multiline_header.

3. Compactor::compact rustdoc reword
   (crates/rig-core/src/memory.rs)

   The original wording said compactor errors were "surfaced as
   MemoryError::Backend" by the composing adapter, which implied
   re-wrapping. CompactingMemory propagates the returned MemoryError
   variant unchanged. The doc paragraph now says errors are
   propagated unchanged and points implementations at Backend (I/O,
   remote-LLM faults) and Internal (invariant breaks) as conventions.

* fix(tools): normalize null tool call arguments to empty object

LLMs frequently send `null` when a tool has all-optional fields and no
arguments are needed. `serde_json::from_str::<T>("null")` fails for

* feat(openrouter): add prompt-caching support for Anthropic models

Adds opt-in Anthropic-style prompt caching for Anthropic models routed through
OpenRouter. When enabled, the outgoing request body is post-processed to
convert the system-prompt content into a structured text block with
`cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}`. Anthropic caches this prefix at

system prompt hit the cache and are billed at the reduced rate. Non-Anthropic
backends routed through OpenRouter ignore the `cache_control` field gracefully.

- Add `apply_prompt_caching(body: &mut Value)` that finds the first system
  message and rewrites its content: string content is converted to a single
  text block with cache_control; array content has cache_control added to the
  last block (non-text blocks such as images are preserved unchanged).
- Add `prompt_caching: bool` field and `with_prompt_caching()` builder to
  `CompletionModel`.
- Wire the post-processing step into both the non-streaming `completion()`
  path and the streaming `stream()` path.
- Four tests: string system message, array system message (last-block only),
  non-text block preservation, and no-system-message no-op.

fix(rig-gemini-grpc): populate FunctionDeclaration.parameters from ToolDefinition (#1763)

* fix(rig-gemini-grpc): populate FunctionDeclaration.parameters from ToolDefinition

create_grpc_request mapped ToolDefinition into proto::FunctionDeclaration
but forwarded only `name` and `description`, leaving `parameters` at the
default `None`. Every tool was therefore sent to Gemini with no argument
shape, degrading tool calls to argument-less invocations.

Add a small JSON Schema -> proto::Schema converter local to this crate
(no rig-core leak), and pipe `tool.parameters` through it inside
create_grpc_request. The empty-object schema
({"type": "object", "properties": {}}) still resolves to None to avoid
emitting a vacuous schema, matching the convention used by
rig-core::providers::gemini::completion.

Tests cover the empty/null shortcut, scalar object properties with
required, typed array items, string enums, and a request-level
assertion that exercises create_grpc_request end-to-end and would have
caught the original regression.

feat(rig-derive): replace hand-rolled schema with schemars in #[rig_tool] (#1576)

* fix(rig-derive): default required to all parameters when not specified

Previously, omitting `required(...)` from `#[rig_tool]` produced an
empty `required` array in the JSON Schema, making all parameters
optional. This silently breaks strict function calling (e.g. OpenAI)
where all params are typically required.

Now all parameters are required by default. Explicit `required(...)`
still works as an override for tools with truly optional params.

* feat(rig-derive): replace hand-rolled schema with schemars in #[rig_tool]

Replace get_json_type() with schemars::JsonSchema derivation on the
generated params struct. Schema is now produced via schema_for!() at
runtime — the same pattern AgentToolArgs already uses.

Key changes:
- Derive JsonSchema on params struct, use schema_for!() in definition()
- Extract doc comments from functions and parameters for descriptions
- Auto-add #[serde(default)] on Option<T> fields
- Strip #[doc] attrs from fn params before re-emitting (compiler rejects them)
- Re-export schemars from rig-core as rig::schemars

Breaking: i32 now produces "type": "integer" (was "number").

Tests: 23 pass covering doc comments, Option<T>, enums, HashMap,
nested structs, Vec, async, visibility, required defaults.

* fix(openai): ensure properties key exists on object schemas in sanitizer

OpenAI rejects object schemas without a "properties" key (400:
"object schema missing properties"), even for zero-parameter tools.
Anthropic accepts bare {"type": "object"} without properties.

Add the missing-properties injection to openai::sanitize_schema,
which also covers Azure since it delegates to the same function.

feat(agent)!: sans-IO AgentRun state machine; both agent loops become thin drivers (#1899)

* feat(agent): add sans-IO AgentRun state machine and port both agent loops onto it

Extract the multi-turn agent loop into an explicit, steppable,
serializable state machine (agent::run::AgentRun) and rewrite both the
non-streaming (PromptRequest::send) and streaming
(StreamingPromptRequest::send) paths as thin drivers over it, removing
the duplicated loop logic that had already drifted between them.

The machine owns every loop decision — turn counting, tool-call
validation, invalid tool-call recovery (fail/retry/repair/skip with
budgets), history threading, usage aggregation, and final response
construction — and performs no IO. Drivers act on AgentRunStep
(CallModel / CallTools / Done) and feed results back, keeping hooks,
memory, tracing spans, and tool execution concurrency at the driver
layer. All state between steps is Serialize + Deserialize, so runs
(streamed ones included) can be suspended while tool calls are pending
and resumed elsewhere.

Streaming reuses the same machine through a sans-IO accumulator
(agent::run::streamed::StreamedTurnAssembler) that assembles incremental
stream items into the same canonical complete turn the non-streaming
path feeds the machine, while still surfacing invalid tool calls
mid-stream so a doomed provider stream can be abandoned early. The
machine's streamed entry points apply the same recovery semantics with
rollback messages built from the partial turn.

Both modules are public: AgentRun can be driven by hand (see
examples/agent_run_stepping.rs) and streamed via the assembler.

Behavior is preserved: the full existing test suite passes unchanged
(only two test-import lines moved). Three unpinned divergences are
resolved toward non-streaming semantics: mid-run cancellation history
now includes the recorded assistant turn, streaming MaxTurnsError
carries the actual pending message instead of its rag-text
reconstruction, and the lost-prompt error string is unified.

* fix(agent): carry pending tool calls in the serialized run state

RunState::ExecutingTools was a unit state: the pending calls existed
only in the AgentRunStep::CallTools value, so a process resuming a
serialized AgentRun could not know which tools to execute — undercutting
the suspend/resume guarantee.

  CallTools idempotently while results are pending (like Done), so a
  resumed process recovers the calls from the run state alone.

  result must be a tool result answering a pending call (multiset match
  on tool call IDs, so duplicate provider IDs stay answerable) and every
  pending call must be answered. Validation failures leave the run
  drivable.

* feat(core)!: drop the Option<Usage> sentinel for unreported token usage

Usage already documents zero-valued metrics as the sentinel for "the
provider supplied no usage", so the Option layer on top of it was a
second encoding of the same fact — kept consistent only by a
normalization convention (reported_usage) that call sites had to
remember. Code review caught one forgetting it.

Following pydantic-ai's usage design (plain integer monoids, zero is
the empty value, request count carried by the per-call records), remove
the sentinel so the invalid state is unrepresentable:

- CompletionCall.usage is now plain Usage; zero means unreported. The
  field deserializes legacy `"usage": null` payloads (covered by
  fixtures captured from the previous format, including a suspended
  AgentRun) but serializes as a plain zero-valued object.
- reported_usage and CompletionCall::from_reported_usage are gone;
  CompletionCall::new takes Usage. PromptResponse::requests() exposes
  the completion-request count.
- GetTokenUsage::token_usage() returns Usage (default when the response
  carries none) across all provider implementations.
- AgentRun::record_streamed_completion_call and
  StreamedTurnEvent::Completed carry plain Usage.
- Telemetry and span recording skip zero-valued usage, preserving the
  previous unset-span-fields behavior for unreported metrics.

BREAKING CHANGE: CompletionCall.usage is Usage instead of
Option<Usage> (serialized form changes from `null` to a zero-valued
object; old payloads still deserialize), CompletionCall::new and
AgentRun::record_streamed_completion_call take Usage, and
GetTokenUsage::token_usage returns Usage. Zero-valued usage everywhere
means the provider reported no metrics, per Usage's documented
sentinel.

ToolSet previously kept a HashMap<String, ToolType> alongside a parallel

docs(examples): add Gemini mid-stream disruption token-counting example (#1918)

Adds a live Gemini example demonstrating how to obtain a token-count
estimate when a streaming generation is disrupted mid-response, for any
reason: manual cancel, transport/server error, premature close, or a
stall/half-open connection.

Gemini only emits authoritative usageMetadata on the final stream chunk,
and there is no cancel flag to send the server, so an interrupted stream
never yields exact usage. The example accumulates output incrementally
and, keyed solely on whether authoritative usage arrived (not on why the
stream stopped), falls back to the free countTokens endpoint to estimate
input/output tokens from the partial output. A per-read timeout turns a
silent stall into the same accounting path.

All four disruption shapes are injected against a real stream via a small
Stream wrapper and funnel into one drain_with_accounting routine.

fix(sqlite): brute-force scan when KNN candidate count exceeds sqlite-vec's k cap (#1920)

sqlite-vec's vec0 KNN query rejects any `k` above a hard-coded 4096
("k value in knn query too large, provided N and the limit is 4096").
`candidate_limit()` can return the full stored embedding count, which is
bound to `k = ?`, so any search over a store with >4096 embeddings fails
whenever a document owns multiple embeddings or a non-indexed
(post-)filter forces exhaustive candidate retrieval. This is reachable
with a small `samples` value (e.g. top_n(10)) and is the cause of #1904.

When the required candidate count exceeds the cap, drop the
`embedding MATCH ?` / `k = ?` constraints and rank every row with the
scalar `vec_distance_*` functions the score expression already uses.
vec0 KNN is itself an exact brute-force scan, so the fallback returns
identical results without the cap (only without the SIMD/chunk fast
path). The fast KNN path is kept for candidate counts within the cap.

Also tightens the multi-embedding candidate bound from the full
embedding count to the exact, tight `samples + (embedding_count -
document_count)`, keeping more queries on the fast KNN path.

Adds unit tests for the path selection / parameter alignment and live
regression tests for both trigger branches (>4096 embeddings via a
multi-embedding document, and an exhaustive post-filter).

Fixes #1904

* fix(rmcp): add configurable, wasm-friendly per-call timeout for MCP tools (#1914)

`McpTool::call` awaited the rmcp peer's `call_tool` with no timeout. When the
StreamableHttp transport orphans an in-flight request during transparent
session re-initialization (server returns HTTP 404 -> the worker's
`streams.abort_all()` cancels the SSE task carrying the outstanding response,
surfacing as `JoinError::Cancelled`), the request never receives a response
and never errors. The peer's `call_tool` future then hangs forever, wedging
the agent loop — which already turns a tool *error* into a tool result the
model can react to, but cannot escape a call that never returns.

Add an optional per-call timeout that converts the unbounded await into a
recoverable `ToolError`:

- `McpTool` gains a `timeout: Option<Duration>` field, with
  `from_mcp_server_with_timeout` / `with_timeout`. `from_mcp_server` keeps its
  signature and defaults to `None`, so existing behavior is unchanged.
- `AgentBuilder::rmcp_tool[s]_with_timeout` and `McpClientHandler::with_timeout`
  expose it through both entry points.
- The timeout uses a new `wasm_compat::timeout` built on `futures_timer::Delay`
  (already used for SSE backoff), not `tokio::time` — rig's `tokio` dep has no
  `time` feature and `tokio::time` does not work on wasm. Verified to compile
  for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

A regression test asserts a configured timeout yields an error instead of
hanging; the existing reproduction confirms the default (no timeout) behavior
is preserved.

fix(ollama): preserve assistant reasoning from non-streaming responses (#1926) (#1927)

* fix(ollama): preserve assistant reasoning from non-streaming responses (#1926)

The non-streaming /api/chat parse (TryFrom<CompletionResponse>) and From<Message>
destructured the response `thinking` but built `choice` from only text +
tool_calls, keeping thinking solely in `raw_response`. So a qwen3-style turn
(content: "", thinking: "...", tool_calls: [...]) produced a choice with no
AssistantContent::Reasoning. The reasoning never entered agent history and was
therefore never echoed back to Ollama on the next turn — which (per Qwen's
function-calling-with-thinking guidance) degrades multi-turn tool-call accuracy.
Streaming already surfaced reasoning via RawStreamingChoice::ReasoningDelta, so
non-streaming agents (the default) were the broken path.

Both conversions now push an AssistantContent::Reasoning when `thinking` is
present, mirroring the streaming path. The send side already serializes
Reasoning -> thinking (test_message_conversion_with_thinking), so reasoning now
round-trips end to end.

Adds a regression test asserting the non-streaming response surfaces Reasoning.
Verified against a live local Ollama + qwen3:4b: before, the tool-call turn's
choice was [ToolCall] (6.8k chars of thinking dropped); after, [Reasoning,
ToolCall] and [Reasoning, Text] across turns. 885 lib tests pass, clippy + fmt clean.

Closes #1926

Adds replayable provider cassette tests for Ollama (a thinking model,

- reasoning_roundtrip (streaming + nonstreaming): multi-turn reasoning is
  accepted back by Ollama on the follow-up turn.
- reasoning_tool_roundtrip (streaming + nonstreaming): the model reasons,
  calls get_weather, and answers from the result. The nonstreaming test
  asserts the assistant's reasoning is preserved in caller-owned chat
  history (assert_chat_history_preserves_reasoning_tool_roundtrip) — the
  direct integration regression for #1926.

Recorded against a local Ollama server (qwen3:4b) and replayed

feat(agent): add OutputMode to compose structured output with tools (#1928) (#1929)

* feat(agent): add OutputMode to compose structured output with tools (#1928)

Applying `output_schema` as the provider's native structured-output
constraint (`format`/`response_format`) on every agent-loop turn suppressed
tool calls: the model emitted schema JSON immediately instead of using its
tools (issue #1928).

Add an `OutputMode` knob (mirrors pydantic-ai) on the agent builder:

- `Auto` (default): resolves to `Tool` when an output schema and >=1 tool are
  present and the tool choice permits the output-tool call, else `Native`.
  Only changes behavior for the tool + schema case that was broken.
- `Tool`: register the schema as a synthetic, collision-safe output tool
  (`final_result`) the model calls to finalize; no native constraint, so the
  model can use its real tools first. The agent loop intercepts the call and
  finalizes with its arguments.
- `Native`: legacy native structured output (the escape hatch).
- `Prompted`: inject the schema into the preamble and parse the model's text
  (for weak/local models).

Wired through both the streaming and non-streaming drivers via the shared
`AgentRun` intercept. Typed prompts (`prompt_typed`) and the `Extractor` pin
`Native` to preserve their existing behavior.

Robustness details:
- The finalizing turn is persisted as the assistant's final text (keeping
  reasoning, dropping the output-tool call) so saved history has no
  unanswered tool_use that providers reject on a later conversation turn.
- Tool mode degrades to `Native` when `tool_choice` forbids the output-tool
  call (`None`/`Specific`), so structured output is enforced, not dropped.
- Once committed, Tool mode is pinned for the run so a per-turn tool-set
  change can't flip back to the native constraint.

Adds unit tests for mode resolution, tool-choice degradation, tool-name
collision handling, and the run intercept (incl. history validity), plus
live-recorded Ollama cassette tests for Tool (streaming and non-streaming),
Native, and Prompted modes.

Closes #1928

* feat(agent): provider-aware OutputMode, output re-prompt/validation, typed unification (#1928)

Addresses review feedback on the OutputMode change.

Provider-aware `Auto`:
- Add `CompletionModel::composes_native_output_with_tools()` (default false;
  true for OpenAI chat-completions/responses and Anthropic, which compose a
  native structured-output constraint with tool calls). `Auto` now routes a
  tool + schema agent to `Tool` only on providers whose native constraint would
  suppress tool calls (e.g. Ollama), and keeps guaranteed `Native` elsewhere.

Stronger Tool-mode contract:
- When the model finalizes without calling the output tool, or calls it with
  arguments missing required schema fields, the run re-prompts a bounded number
  of times (default 1) before finalizing best-effort. If a plain-text turn is
  already valid structured output, it is accepted instead of re-prompting.
- The output-retry budget resets on real-tool progress, so it is per
  finalization attempt rather than a single per-run allowance.

Typed unification:
- `prompt_typed::<T>()` now flows through `OutputMode` like the untyped API
  (was pinned to `Native`); the typed `send()` paths deserialize tolerantly,
  stripping prose / markdown fences around the JSON.

Robustness:
- Tool mode is pinned for the run via the persisted `output_tool_name`, so the
  pin survives a serialize/resume and a tool-less first turn can still resolve
  to Tool once tools appear (only Tool is pinned; Native/Prompted re-resolve).
- Warn when a real tool collides with the synthetic output-tool name mid-run.

Docs corrected: `Prompted` returns the model's text (caller parses); `Tool`
and `Prompted` are best-effort; `Auto` is provider-aware.

Adds unit tests for provider-aware resolution, the re-prompt/validation loops,
valid-text acceptance, and fence-tolerant typed deserialization.

* fix(agent): keep prompt_typed pinned to Native (#1928)

Routing the typed path through OutputMode (so tool-using typed agents on
non-composing providers use Tool mode) changed typed + tools behavior from the
native structured-output constraint to a synthetic output tool. That broke the
typed + tools cassettes of every OpenAI-compatible provider (copilot,
openrouter, xai, groq, llamacpp, llamafile, …), which were recorded under the
native path and can't be re-recorded here.

Re-pin `prompt_typed::<T>()` to `Native` so the typed API behaves identically
across all providers, and leave routing typed output through Tool mode as a
follow-up. The untyped `output_schema`/`output_mode` API still composes
structured output with tools; provider-aware `Auto`, the Tool-mode
re-prompt/validation, and the robustness fixes are unchanged.

The fence-tolerant typed deserializer is kept as a safety net.

* fix(agent): streaming Tool-mode returns structured output, not prose (#1928)

The streaming finalize gated output re-sourcing on the turn having no assistant
text. A Tool-mode finishing turn that emits BOTH prose and the output-tool call
therefore fell through and surfaced the prose as the final `response()` while
keeping the output-tool call in `content()` — an unanswered tool_use and a
divergence from the non-streaming result (which always returns the structured
output).

Gate on the presence of the output-tool call instead (any tool call at `Done`
is the output tool — real calls route to `CallTools`): drop the tool call and
the prose, keep reasoning, and append the run's output as the final text.
Extracted as `finalize_streamed_choice` with a unit test covering the
prose-plus-tool-call case the cassette did not exercise.

ci: run doctests and stop rig-sqlite opting out of them (#1939)

`cargo nextest` (used by the `test` job) does not run doctests by design,
and the `doc` job only *builds* documentation — so no CI job ever executed
the `///` code examples. A doctest that fails to compile (or panics when
run) sails straight through with CI green.

rig-sqlite compounded this: it set `[lib] doctest = false`, excluding its
examples from `cargo test --doc` entirely — even though #1716 set doctests
to true project-wide specifically to keep examples from going stale.

- Add a `doctest` CI job running `cargo test --doc --workspace --all-features`.
- Flip rig-sqlite's `doctest = false` -> `true` so its examples are tested
  alongside everyone else's.

All existing doctests pass — verified per-crate in isolation (19/19) and
across the full workspace with `--all-features` — so this is preventive: it
closes the hole before a broken example can land. Confirmed effective by
temporarily breaking a rig-sqlite example and watching `cargo test --doc`
fail, which it previously could not.

fix(rig-core): fix epub loader tests + prevent CWD-relative fixture-path regressions (#1940)

* fix(rig-core): resolve loader test fixtures via a CWD-independent helper

The epub loader tests globbed `tests/data/*.epub` relative to the process
working directory. The crate reorg (#1699) moved the fixture from
`rig-core/tests/data/dummy.epub` to the workspace-root `tests/data/`, so
`cargo test -p rig-core` (which runs with CWD = the crate root) globbed the
non-existent `crates/rig-core/tests/data/`, matched zero files, and the four
content assertions failed with `left: 0, right: 1`.

The pdf loader tests had already been fixed by anchoring fixtures to
`CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`; the epub tests were simply missed. Extract that pattern
into a shared `loaders::test_fixtures` helper and route both the pdf and epub
tests through it, so fixture paths resolve regardless of the runner's working
directory (`cargo test` uses the crate root, `cargo nextest` the workspace
root — which is why CI never surfaced this).

Fixes 4 tests under `cargo test -p rig-core --all-features`:
- loaders::epub::loader::tests::test_epub_loader_with_errors
- loaders::epub::loader::tests::test_epub_loader_with_ignoring_errors
- loaders::epub::loader::tests::test_single_file
- loaders::epub::loader::tests::test_single_file_with_path

* ci: reject CWD-relative test fixture paths

`cargo test` runs tests from the crate root while `cargo nextest` (CI's
runner) runs from the workspace root, so a bare `tests/data/...` fixture path
passes under one runner and fails under the other — a broken path can stay

feat(rig-core)!: integrate hooks into AgentRun via a composable AgentRunner (#1945)

* feat(rig-core)!: integrate hooks into AgentRun via a composable AgentRunner

The sans-IO `AgentRun` state machine and the `PromptHook` system were
disjoint: hooks were welded into the private `PromptRequest` /
`StreamingPromptRequest` send loops, so hand-driving `AgentRun` had no hook
support and the two driver loops duplicated the same drive logic.

Introduce `AgentRunner<M>`, a reusable hook-aware driver that pairs the
unchanged serializable `AgentRun` with model IO, tool execution, memory and
hooks. `run()` (blocking) and `stream()` (incremental) share one drive loop,
one run-construction site (`build_agent_run`) and one tool-execution path
(`run_single_tool`), so they behave identically apart from the inherently
streamed delta events. `agent.prompt(..)` and `agent.stream_prompt(..)` are
thin wrappers over it; `agent.runner(prompt)` exposes the same loop for custom
control flow.

Replace the 8-method `PromptHook` with a single-method, composable
`AgentHook<M>`:

  async fn on_event(&self, event: StepEvent<'_, M>) -> Flow

`StepEvent` carries one variant per observable point (completion call/response,
invalid tool call, tool call/result, streaming text/tool-call deltas, stream
finish); `Flow` unifies the old `HookAction` / `ToolCallHookAction` /
invalid-tool recovery. Hooks compose via `HookStack`: `add_hook` appends (call
it again to stack more), and the first to return a non-Continue `Flow` wins.

Hardening from review:
- Fail-closed `Flow`: an action an event cannot honor (e.g. `Flow::Fail` on a
  tool call) terminates the run instead of silently proceeding, so a blocking
  hook can never fail open.
- Skip reasons (and the streamed invalid-tool skip) are emitted verbatim, never
  re-parsed as structured/multimodal tool output — matched across both drivers.
- `AgentHook::observes(StepEventKind)` lets a hook opt out of high-frequency
  delta events; the runner skips building/dispatching them, so an empty stack
  and tool-only hooks pay nothing per delta.
- The `agent::hook` module docs carry a method-by-method `PromptHook` →
  `AgentHook` migration table (each old method → its `StepEvent` variant and the
  `Flow` to return), since this is a clean break with no shim.
- The blocking tool loop no longer deep-clones the whole conversation per tool
  call: the diagnostic history (only read on a hook-terminate error path) is
  materialized once and shared by borrow, so the common success path does no
  per-tool history copying.
- Response-finish parity on recovered turns. A turn that streamed text *and*
  emitted an invalid tool call that a hook repaired is a recovered turn: the
  blocking driver already suppresses its `CompletionResponse` hook, but the
  streaming driver fired `StreamResponseFinish` anyway. The streaming path now
  suppresses it the same way (tracking `turn_recovered`, mirroring blocking's
  `response_hook_suppressed`); the streamed final item is still yielded, so
  output and history are unchanged. A dedicated test pins the suppression on
  both drivers (the shared-events harness excludes these medium-specific events
  by design, so it could not catch the asymmetry).
- Parity and composition tests. A single-source-of-truth differential harness
  derives BOTH the blocking and streaming mock models from one canonical
  `ScriptedTurn` list (the pydantic-ai `TestModel` / litellm `stream_chunk_builder`
  principle), so the two drivers cannot be fed divergent behavior, and drives it
  through `run()` and `stream()` in two wire shapes (complete tool calls and
  name/argument deltas — "chunked-input invariance"), asserting identical output,
  message history, tool-result content and hook event sequence. Scenarios cover
  text-only, single-tool, multi-tool-in-one-turn and multi-turn runs, plus
  invalid-tool repair and skip recovery. `Flow::Terminate` is shown fail-closed
  from each shared event on both drivers; a two-hook stack is checked for parity
  across drivers; and `HookStack` is unit-tested directly for registration order,
  first-non-Continue short-circuit, OR-combined `observes`, and the empty-stack
  no-op.

BREAKING CHANGE: `PromptHook`, `HookAction` and `ToolCallHookAction` are
removed in favor of `AgentHook` / `StepEvent` / `Flow`. `Agent`, `AgentBuilder`
and the prompt-request types drop their hook type parameter `P` (hooks are now
a runtime `HookStack<M>`); `AgentBuilder::hook(..)` becomes `add_hook(..)`, an
append-only method (there is no stack-replacing setter — hooks always compose).
`InvalidToolCallContext` and `InvalidToolCallHookAction`
(used when hand-driving `AgentRun::resolve_invalid_tool_call`) are retained.

Builder/runner method names are aligned for consistency:
`AgentBuilder::conversation_id(..)` becomes `conversation(..)` (matching
`PromptRequest`/`AgentRunner::conversation`), and the runner/request builders
drop the lone `with_` prefix — `with_history(..)` -> `history(..)` and
`with_tool_concurrency(..)` -> `tool_concurrency(..)`. The lower-level
`AgentRun::with_history(..)`, part of its own `with_`-prefixed builder family,
is unchanged.

feat(openai-responses)!: preserve unknown Output payloads (#1950)

* feat(openai-responses): preserve unknown Output payloads

`Output::Unknown` was a fieldless variant, so every unrecognized
Responses-API output item decoded to a unit and the payload was
discarded. Provider-native hosted tools (`web_search_call`,
`file_search_call`, `computer_use_call`, `code_interpreter_call`)
arrive as exactly these unknown items, so their data was destroyed at
the typed-decode boundary and never reached a `PromptHook` or consumer.

Carry the raw `serde_json::Value` through the catch-all:
`Output::Unknown` -> `Output::Unknown(Value)`. `#[serde(other)]` only
applies to a unit variant, so the (de)serialization is hand-written and
dispatches known `type` tags through a private `KnownOutput` mirror; the
internally tagged wire shape of the known variants is unchanged, and a
known tag with a malformed body still errors rather than silently
degrading to `Unknown`. The enum also gains `#[non_exhaustive]`.

This preserves the original invariant the catch-all was added for —
unknown item types must not break `CompletionResponse` decoding or drop
token usage — while no longer discarding the payload.

BREAKING CHANGE: `Output::Unknown` now carries a `serde_json::Value`.
Exhaustive matches need `Output::Unknown(_)`.

* refactor(openai-responses): serialize Output without cloning known payloads

Address PR review: serialize known Output variants through a borrowed
KnownOutputRef mirror instead of cloning into the owned KnownOutput, and
rename output_unknown_round_trips_byte_stable to _value_equal to match the
serde_json::Value equality it asserts.

* refactor(openai-responses): hand-write Output serde Citation-style, drop non_exhaustive

Refines the unknown-Output-payload work to match the existing house pattern
(Anthropic's `Citation`) and to address review feedback on #1855.

- Hand-write `Output`'s `Serialize`/`Deserialize` directly against the payload
  types instead of through mirror enums. Deserialize dispatches on the `type`
  tag into `OutputMessage` / `OutputFunctionCall` / a `ReasoningFields` helper;
  an unmodeled tag — including an absent or non-string one — becomes
  `Unknown(value)`, while a modeled tag with a malformed body still errors.
  Serialize emits each modeled payload's fields plus the internally tagged
  `type`, and `Unknown` re-emits its raw value. Deletes the `KnownOutput` and
  `KnownOutputRef` mirror enums and the `From<KnownOutput>` impl. Mirrors
  `Citation` (anthropic/completion.rs).
- Drop `#[non_exhaustive]` from `Output`. `Unknown(Value)` already delivers the
  forward-compat; `#[non_exhaustive]` is an extra SemVer break with no precedent
  among provider enums, and `Citation` (the same pattern) is not
  `#[non_exhaustive]` either.
- Drop the redundant `#[serde(alias = "function_call")]` (snake_case already
  yields that tag).
- Tests: add the high-value `Output::Reasoning { encrypted_content: Some, status:
  Some }` round-trip (field parity + the reasoning dispatch arm), a per-tag
  decode guard (every modeled `type` resolves to its variant, never `Unknown`),
  and an absent/non-string `type` case. Round-trips assert value-equality (the
  hand-written serialize appends `type`, so it is value-equal, not
  byte-for-byte).
- Document at the streaming/copilot `Unknown` arms that the preserved payload is
  not yet surfaced to streaming consumers (it is reachable on
  `CompletionResponse.output`); add a `[**breaking**]` CHANGELOG entry.

Refs #1855, #1861.

fix(openai-compat): normalize evicted tool-call string arguments to an object (#1958)

The streaming tool-call eviction path (distinct-named tool calls within a
single assistant turn) only normalized a `null` arguments value to `{}` and
otherwise passed the value through verbatim. Because OpenAI-compatible
tool-call arguments accumulate as a JSON *string* (`Value::String`), an
evicted call leaked a bare string into `ToolCall.function.arguments`. A
downstream serializer that expects an object (e.g. the Anthropic protocol's
`tool_use.input`) then emitted a string, which strict providers reject with
`tool_use.input: Input should be a valid dictionary`.

Mirror `finalize_pending_tool_call`: parse a string payload into the
underlying object, with empty/unparseable/non-object payloads normalized to
`{}` so the downstream input is always a dictionary.

Adds regression coverage: string->object, null/empty/non-object->{}, and an
end-to-end test that the eviction path emits object `tool_use` input.

* feat(rig-core): steer the model request per turn from a hook via Flow::OverrideRequest

A hook can now return `Flow::OverrideRequest { request }` for a
`StepEvent::CompletionCall` to patch the model request before it is sent — the
prepareStep-equivalent. Constructor `Flow::override_request(..)` + a builder
`RequestOverride`.

`RequestOverride` is a partial patch (all fields `Option`, built with setters):
preamble, temperature, max_tokens, tool_choice, active_tools (a by-name allow-list
that narrows the advertised tool set), and additional_params (shallow-merged onto

non-sticky and never mutates the agent baseline. Use it to force a tool on the
first turn, lower temperature on a critical step, or shrink the tool set after a
phase.

in the shared `build_prepared_completion_request`, so it behaves identically on
the blocking and streaming drivers. The variant is additive (`Flow` is
`#[non_exhaustive]`); because the override carries an `f64` temperature, `Flow` is
now `PartialEq` and no longer `Eq` (nothing relied on `Flow: Eq`).

* fix(examples): make the HITL approval gate fail-closed + strengthen tests

Review of the example surfaced that the approval gate was fail-OPEN, which is
exactly wrong for a gate guarding side-effecting tools (send_email, delete_file):
- an empty line, an unrecognized choice (e.g. "n"/"no"/typo), and closed stdin
  (piped `< /dev/null`, Ctrl-D) all mapped to approve;
- decisions were matched on the first char only, so typing the word "abort"
  (first char 'a') was read as "approve" — trying to stop a deletion triggered it.

Now the gate fails closed: `ask` returns Option (None on EOF/error), the whole
lowercased answer is matched (hotkey or full word, so "abort" can't be mistaken
for "approve"), empty/unknown input denies, and closed stdin aborts the run. A
note clarifies the prompt is a UX affordance, not a security boundary.

fix(anthropic): coerce tool_use.input to an object at the send boundary (#1964)

The Anthropic API requires `tool_use.input` to be a JSON object and rejects
anything else with a deterministic 400:
`messages.N.content.M.tool_use.input: Input should be a valid dictionary`.

Both assistant-content conversion sites (`Message::try_from` and
`anthropic_content_from_assistant_content`) forwarded
`ToolCall.function.arguments` verbatim into `Content::ToolUse { input, .. }`.
`arguments` is provider-shaped `serde_json::Value`: depending on how the
turn was built (replayed history, an evicted streamed tool call, a provider
that accumulates arguments as a JSON string), it can arrive as a
`Value::String`, `Value::Null`, or another non-object. Anthropic then
rejects the whole multi-turn request, which breaks every tool conversation
on Anthropic-shaped endpoints (including third-party gateways that speak the
Anthropic protocol).

This is the Anthropic-serialization counterpart of the openai-compat
eviction fix (#1958): #1958 stops a string leaking out of the eviction
source; this normalizes at the Anthropic send boundary so the contract
holds no matter how `arguments` was produced upstream.

`coerce_tool_input`:
- object -> passed through unchanged
- JSON string encoding an object -> parsed into that object
- non-JSON string / non-object JSON string / null / array / number / bool
  -> `{}` (the only shape the API accepts)

Adds unit coverage for each branch.

over one `drive_agent` engine; this pass removes the incidental plumbing still
duplicated across the two surfaces (naming the seams #1985 exposed) and fixes
one live provider drift bug. It deliberately stops short of the two *essential*
divergences (the `CompletionModel` two-associated-types split and the blocking-vs-
streaming invalid-tool-call recovery semantics), which are load-bearing and must
survive.

Steps (each behavior-preserving except step 4, a reviewed provider-wire fix):

1. `AgentRun::record_completion_call` + `finalize_turn` seams — both ingestion
   paths already ended at a byte-identical `AwaitingAdvance(TurnState { .. })`, and
   the `CompletionCall::new; idx+=1; push; usage+=` arithmetic was copied 3x. The
   once-per-turn `streamed_completion_call_recorded` guard stays OUTSIDE the helper
   so it can't be mistaken for "a completion call happened". `Usage::new()` is the
   additive identity, so the no-usage fallback routes through it unchanged.

2. `forward_prompt_setters!` builder macro — collapses the 6 identical setters
   (docs and all) shared by the blocking `PromptRequest` and `TypedPromptRequest`.
   Scoped to those two (identical docs); the streaming builder keeps its
   medium-specific setter docs. `max_turns` is added to `StreamingPromptRequest` as
   an additive alias of `multi_turn` (no deprecation — `multi_turn` has 40+ in-crate
   call sites).

3. `emit_completion_call!` macro — collapses the two substantive completion-call
   emission sites in `StreamingTurnSource::run_model_turn`. The macro returns the
   item/None/error; the `yield` stays at the call site because `async_stream::stream!`
   cannot see a `yield` produced inside a nested macro expansion. The trivial
   no-usage fallback stays inline (it must not set the now-dead flag).

4. Anthropic single request builder (fixes a live bug) — streaming derived its body
   from a hand-assembled `json!` that had drifted from the blocking typed request
   and silently dropped `output_schema` (structured-output config). It now goes
   through the same `AnthropicCompletionRequest` + `stream: true`. `default_max_tokens`
   pre-resolution is preserved (the typed `TryFrom` errors on `None`). This changes
   emitted `tool_choice`/`output_config` bytes to match the blocking path — a reviewed
   parity fix, pinned by a new test asserting streaming body == blocking body + stream.

5. `unknown_tool_call_error` leaf helper — collapses the 9 identical
   `PromptError::UnknownToolCall { .. }` constructions across both recovery functions
   and the streamed fail-fast. Control flow, recovery semantics, and — critically —
   the streamed fail-fast staying a real release-mode `return Err` are untouched.

6. `build_chat_span!` macro — the identical 15-field chat span was duplicated in
   both `TurnSource::open_chat_span` impls. A macro (not a fn) because `tracing`
   requires a static span-name literal; the two distinct names (`chat` /
   `chat_streaming`, which dashboards split on) are preserved.

* fix(anthropic): keep streaming tool_choice:auto default; fmt

The Step 4 unification switched the Anthropic streaming body to the blocking
typed request, which omits `tool_choice` when unset. Recorded streaming cassettes
(and the established streaming wire format) expect the explicit `tool_choice: auto`
the hand-rolled body always sent when tools are advertised but the choice is unset
— equivalent to Anthropic's default, but a real request-byte change that broke
`multi_turn_streaming_tools` and `messages_adaptive_thinking_streaming_tool_roundtrip_smoke`.

Re-apply the explicit `auto` after deriving from the typed request so the streaming
bytes stay stable, while still fixing the actual bug (the dropped `output_schema` /
structured-output config) and keeping the two paths deduplicated. Add a unit test
pinning the preserved `tool_choice: auto`. Also apply rustfmt to the test-module
import block.

* fix(anthropic): drop streaming tool_choice when no tools are advertised

Code review of the Step 4 rewrite found a behavioral change: the old hand-rolled
streaming body emitted `tool_choice` only inside `if !tools.is_empty()` (Anthropic
rejects `tool_choice` without `tools`), but deriving from the typed
`AnthropicCompletionRequest` serializes any caller-set `tool_choice` regardless of
the tool set, and the re-apply guard only *added* `auto` — it never *stripped* a
stray `tool_choice`. So a streaming request with `tool_choice = Some(..)` and no
tools (reachable via a per-turn `Flow::OverrideRequest` or a misconfigured agent)
now put `tool_choice` on the wire without `tools`, which Anthropic 400s.

Make the reconciliation complete and symmetric — `tool_choice` appears iff a
non-empty tool set is advertised: tools present + unset -> explicit `auto`; tools
absent -> drop it. This runs on the serialized body *after* the typed request's
`TryFrom`, so fail-closed `tool_choice` validation (e.g. multi-name `Specific`)
still fires exactly as before, even when tools are empty. Add a test pinning the
strip.

Release-N cleanup: correctness fixes + dead-code removal (#1987)

* fix(vector-store): honor filter + threshold in in-memory index; fix Filter::satisfies field matching

InMemoryVectorIndex::top_n/top_n_ids ignored req.filter() and req.threshold(),
so the default store returned unfiltered/un-thresholded results that diverged
from every real backend. Apply both during the scan (before top-n selection).

Filter::satisfies compared a single-key {k:v} object against the whole document
(only matching single-field docs) and passed an object to compare_pair for
Gt/Lt (always None -> always false). Rewrite leaf filters to look the key up in
the document and compare the field, which also fixes rig-helixdb's use of it.

Add unit tests for satisfies and a top_n filter/threshold conformance test.

* fix(embeddings): de-duplicate VectorDistance impls; fix chebyshev rayon drift

distance.rs carried two full copies of the VectorDistance impl (sequential and
rayon). They had drifted: under the rayon feature, chebyshev_distance used
sequential .iter() while every sibling used par_iter(), so one metric was
silently unparallelized. Factor both impls through one macro parameterized by
the iterator constructor and the max-reduction (Iterator::fold vs
ParallelIterator::reduce), which is why the copy could not simply swap iter for
par_iter. Verified identical results under both feature configs.

* fix(streaming): derive usage from final response in From impl; add usage() accessor

From<StreamingCompletionResponse<R>> for CompletionResponse hardcoded
Usage::new(), so any caller using .into() on a completed stream silently got
zero usage even though R: GetTokenUsage and value.response holds the final
usage. Derive it via Option<R>: GetTokenUsage (zero sentinel when no final
response). Add StreamingCompletionResponse::usage() and cover both paths.

* refactor(core): delete unwired abstractions; dedupe UNKNOWN_AGENT_NAME

Remove speculative/dead code with no consumers anywhere in the workspace:
- Transport::NdJson (never constructed; all matches use wildcards)
- ConvertMessage trait (no impls, no consumer, not re-exported)
- telemetry ProviderRequestExt trait + its lone openai impl (no consumer)
- SpanCombinator::record_model_input (zero call sites)
- http SSE with_retry_policy + RetryPolicy::{Constant,Never} (never used; the
  RetryPolicy trait, ExponentialBackoff, and DEFAULT_RETRY stay)

Dedupe the duplicated UNKNOWN_AGENT_NAME const (agent/runner.rs and
agent/completion.rs) into one pub(crate) const in agent/mod.rs.

* fix(vector-store): address code-review findings on filter/threshold

- Filter::satisfies: make Eq numeric-aware (5 matches 5.0) so equality is
  consistent with Gt/Lt, and compare integers exactly (i64/u64 before f64) so
  values beyond 2^53 no longer collapse to the same lossy f64.
- In-memory scan: exclude non-finite (NaN) similarities from a zero-magnitude
  embedding, which sorted as the OrderedFloat maximum and slipped past the
  threshold check, wrongly ranking #1.
- De-duplicate the per-document scoring block (filter + best similarity +
  finite + threshold) into a shared score_candidate helper used by both the
  brute-force and LSH scans.
- Add regression tests for int/float equality, large-integer ordering, and
  NaN exclusion.

* fix(vector-store): rank documents by best finite embedding

The prior NaN guard ran after max_by, but NaN sorts as the OrderedFloat
maximum, so for a document with multiple embeddings max_by selected the
degenerate (zero-magnitude) chunk and the guard then dropped the whole
document — even when it had a strong finite-similarity chunk. Filter
non-finite similarities before max_by so a document ranks by its best finite
embedding and is skipped only when it has none. Add a multi-embedding
regression test.
feat(ollama): Extend `think` options with `max` (#1982)

fix(ollama): omit `think` when unset so the model default applies (#1990)

The Ollama provider always serialized a `think` field, defaulting it to
`false` when the caller did not set one. Ollama's /api/chat treats
`think` as tri-state: an absent field means 'use the model's default',
`false` suppresses thinking, and `true`/level forces it. By always
sending `false`, rig turned off thinking that a model would otherwise
do by default, and there was no way to express the neutral absent state.

Make OllamaCompletionRequest.think an Option<Think> with
skip_serializing_if = 'Option::is_none', so a request built without an
explicit `think` omits the field entirely. Explicit
`think: true | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'` requests are unaffected.

Evolve the agent hook system into a composable middleware layer ahead of
the vector-store/RAG rework, without touching vector stores.

- HookContext: run-scoped context (run_id, turn, is_streaming, agent_name,
  shared Scratchpad) passed to every on_event; breaks the trait signature.
- Mergeable request patches: RequestOverride -> RequestPatch,
  Flow::OverrideRequest -> Flow::PatchRequest. CompletionCall patches from
  every hook accumulate and merge in registration order (no more first-patch
  short-circuit); documented per-field merge rules.
- RequestPatch::extra_context: per-turn passive-RAG document injection,
  appended after static + dynamic context.
- RequestPatch::history: per-turn replacement of the messages sent to the
  provider; transcript untouched, RAG keys off the original history.
- Chained tool rewrites: RewriteArgs/RewriteResult compose across a HookStack.
- StepEvent::ModelTurnFinished: normalized once-per-turn event on both
  surfaces (covers streamed tool-only turns).

All merge/patch/context/history/event semantics land once in the shared
drive loop, so run() and stream() behave identically. Fail-closed handling,
invalid-tool-call recovery, and run-all-then-decide tool execution unchanged.

Review found the pre-v2 'first non-Continue short-circuits the rest' blanket
claim still on all four public add_hook rustdocs and the foundational CHANGELOG
bullet — false for CompletionCall (accumulate) and ToolCall/ToolResult (chain).

* fix(agent): tool termination fail-fast, redaction ordering, canonical ModelTurnFinished

Address the second adversarial review round:

- Flow::Terminate from a tool hook is now turn-wide fail-fast. Sequential
  execution stops before starting remaining siblings; concurrent execution
  drops not-yet-started siblings (a shared flag makes them skip) while draining
  already-in-flight ones, so no new side effect runs after a termination and the
  lowest call-index terminate reason still wins deterministically. Avoids the
  Semantic-Kernel run-all-then-decide fail-open.
- Tool-result redaction: gen_ai.tool.call.result is recorded only AFTER the
  ToolResult hook runs (replacement on RewriteResult, raw on Keep, nothing on
  Terminate), so a redaction hook never leaks the raw output to the trace/logs.
- Streaming ModelTurnFinished.content now carries the canonical committed
  StreamedTurn::choice (reasoning->text->tool ordering), not the raw
  stream.choice aggregate; raw is kept for final stream behavior.
- Scratchpad/HookContext docs: drop "never contends"; document that at
  tool_concurrency > 1 tool hooks for different tools share the context and run
  concurrently, update is race-free per op but imposes no ordering; recommend
  commutative/idempotent state or keying by call id.
- Docs/test hygiene: CHANGELOG old signature includes ctx; anthropic
  request_override wording; () observes nothing; streaming transcript-untouched
  assertion.

non-leak (span capture), canonical ModelTurnFinished ordering — all verified to

* test(agent): genuinely exercise in-flight-drain vs beyond-window-drop; fix () observes doc

Round-2 review follow-ups (both low-severity accuracy fixes):
- The concurrent drop test's narrative was wrong: a synchronous terminator meant

  beyond-window-drop distinction it described. Rewrite with a Notify so tc1 is

  dropped (called never contains 2) and tc0's body never runs. Renamed

- Correct the () hook observes() doc: observes gates only the two streaming delta

* feat(agent)!: split tool-call stream events, atomic tool batches, local tool-choice validation

Round-3 redesign for correctness and cleaner semantics (breaking):

1. Split model-emitted tool call from execution start. StreamAssistantItem
   (StreamedAssistantContent::ToolCall) now reports the tool call the MODEL
   emitted (at turn commit, whether or not it runs). A new
   MultiTurnStreamItem::ToolExecutionStart marks that Rig actually started
   executing a tool (after hook checks) — never for a dropped/hook-skipped/
   invalid-recovery call. run_single_tool now reports `executed` to distinguish

2. Atomic per-batch commit/surface. drive_tool_calls collects tool outcomes
   instead of streaming them one-by-one; execution-start + result items are

feat(tool)!: structured tool-execution results (#2015)

* feat(tool)!: structured tool-execution results

Tool calls now resolve to a structured `ToolExecutionResult { model_output,
outcome, extensions }` that flows through the dynamic tool boundary all the way
to the `StepEvent::ToolResult` hook, so hooks, tracing, telemetry, and policies
can reason about *what happened* without parsing the model-visible string.

- `ToolOutcome` = Success / Error(ToolFailure) / Skipped / Denied, where
  `ToolFailure { kind, message, retryable, code, http_status }` classifies the
  failure via a standard `ToolFailureKind` (InvalidArgs, Timeout, Cancelled,
  NotFound, PermissionDenied, RateLimited, Provider, Network, Other).
- Authoring: `Tool::classify_error` maps a tool's own error type to a
  `ToolFailure` (no string parsing); `Tool::call_structured` returns a
  `ToolReturn<T>` to attach an outcome and/or never-sent-to-the-model
  `ToolResultExtensions` metadata. Plain `T: Serialize` output stays ergonomic.
- Boundary: `ToolDyn`/`ToolType`/`ToolSet`/`ToolServerHandle` gain
  `call_structured`; the shared `run_single_tool` drives it, so blocking and
  streaming observe identical outcomes. MCP tools classify timeout/transport
  errors structurally.
- Hooks: `StepEvent::ToolResult` gains `outcome` + `extensions`. `RewriteResult`
  rewrites only the model-visible text; the raw outcome is unaffected.

Behavioral changes: `Flow::Skip` now fires `ToolResult` with a `Skipped`
outcome; a tool error's model-visible text is now the tool's own `Display`
(formatted at the boundary) rather than the old triple-wrapped string.

Adds regression tests (blocking + streaming), a `tool_result_outcomes` example
(timeout counting + 404 recovery), and docs.

* fix(tool): correctness fixes for structured tool results

Addresses review findings on the structured tool-result system:

- RewriteArgs + Skip: a rewrite from an earlier ToolCall hook was dropped
  when a later hook returned Flow::Skip, so the skipped ToolResult (and
  span) reported the model's original args — leaking un-redacted args.
  HookStack::resolve_tool_call now salvages the accumulated rewrite through
  a short-circuit; run_single_tool applies it to args + tracing in every
  path. The tool still doesn't run and emits no ToolExecutionStart.

- MCP invalid JSON args: McpTool::execute silently coerced malformed JSON
  into a no-argument call. It now classifies malformed args as
  ToolFailureKind::InvalidArgs before contacting the server, preserving
  valid object/null/empty behavior.

- Denied vs Skipped: clarified docs — hook/approval-policy Flow::Skip is
  Skipped; Denied is only produced by a tool via ToolReturn::denied.

Also: Send+Sync guard for ToolExecutionResult; call_tool_structured
success/NotFound tests; fix pre-existing intra-doc-link errors (private
TypeMap links, redundant explicit targets) that failed the doc build.
Adds blocking+streaming regression tests for every behavioral fix.

* fix(agent): preserve tool-arg rewrites across nested HookStacks

A nested HookStack was dispatched as a single hook via `on_event`, which
returns only one `Flow`. So an inner `[RewriteArgs, Skip/Terminate]` lost
its rewrite, and the skipped ToolResult (and span) reported the model's
original args instead of the rewritten ones — leaking un-redacted args.

Make tool-call resolution recursive through composition:
- add a doc-hidden `AgentHook::resolve_tool_call` extension point (default:
  dispatch the ToolCall to `on_event`, no salvaged rewrite — a leaf hook
  can rewrite or short-circuit, never both);
- add object-safe `DynAgentHook::resolve_tool_call_boxed`;
- `HookStack` overrides `resolve_tool_call` to consult members via that
  method and adopt a member's salvaged rewrite before handling its flow, so
  an inner rewrite survives an inner short-circuit at any nesting depth.

`on_event`/`run_single_tool` are unchanged; boxing cost is identical.
Adds nested-composition unit tests (rewrite+skip/terminate/fail-closed,
outer-rewrite+nested-skip, deeply nested, proceeding rewrite) and an
end-to-end blocking+streaming test asserting the skipped ToolResult reports
the rewritten args.

* refactor(tool)!: make tool-authored Skipped unrepresentable

`ToolOutcome` conflated two value sets: what a tool declares (it ran →
Success/Error/Denied) and what the framework observes (adds the
hook-`Flow::Skip` outcome Skipped). Nothing stopped a tool from returning
`ToolOutcome::Skipped` (via `ToolReturn::new`/`with_outcome` or the public
`ToolExecutionResult` field), producing a result that claims to have been
skipped while having actually run, and making `is_skipped()` ambiguous.

Encode the invariant in the type system instead of documenting around it:

- add `ToolReturnOutcome` { Success, Error(ToolFailure), Denied } — a strict
  subset of `ToolOutcome` with no `Skipped` variant — plus `From` into the
  observed `ToolOutcome`;
- `ToolReturn<T>.outcome` is now `ToolReturnOutcome`, so a tool return can
  never be `Skipped`;
- encapsulate `ToolExecutionResult`: fields are `pub(crate)` with
  `model_output()`/`outcome()`/`extensions()` accessors, `new`/`skipped` are
  `pub(crate)`, and the public constructors are only success/failed/denied —
  so a manual `ToolDyn` impl also cannot inject `Skipped`.

`ToolOutcome::Skipped` remains matchable by hooks but is producible only
inside the crate. `is_skipped()` now unambiguously means "a hook skipped it."
Adds tests for the `ToolReturnOutcome` → `ToolOutcome` mapping.

* fix(tool): preserve declared outcome/extensions on output serialize failure

Review of PR #2015 against the reference frameworks surfaced one real bug:
`ToolReturn::into_execution_result` discarded the tool's declared outcome
AND extensions when the output failed to serialize, unconditionally
returning `Error(Other)` with empty extensions. A handled failure or denial
carrying a non-serializable output (e.g. a map with struct keys) was thus
silently reclassified — `is_denied()`/`is_error_kind()` would lie — defeating
the point of structured outcomes. A serialization failure is a rendering
problem: it is now independent of the classification. The declared outcome
and extensions are preserved and only `model_output` falls back to the error
string; only a declared `Success` that cannot be rendered becomes `Other`.

Also from the review:
- add `ToolExecutionResult::with_extension` (single-insert) to match
  `ToolReturn::with_extension` for the manual `ToolDyn` path;
- soften the `tool_result_outcomes` example doc: `main` drives the
  404-recovery half; the timeout-abort branch is implemented but not
  exercised by the single prompt (kept deterministic).

Adds a regression test covering failed/denied/success serialize-failure paths.

docs(examples): add force_tool_first_turn hook example (#2014)

* docs(examples): add force_tool_first_turn hook example

Demonstrates a per-turn RequestPatch footgun and its fix. A RequestPatch is
per-turn and re-fires on every turn, so an AgentHook that patches
tool_choice = Required on every CompletionCall forces a tool call on every turn
— the model never gets a turn to stop calling tools and answer, so the run loops
until max_turns and fails with MaxTurnsError.

The example runs that footgun first (catching the MaxTurnsError), then the fix:
gate the patch on ctx.turn() == 1 so the tool is forced only on the first turn
and later turns resolve normally. Registered as a workspace example and listed in
examples/README.md. Requires OPENAI_API_KEY to run.
