* feat(streaming): drivers check sequence laws against raw adapter output in debug builds

The lifecycle laws lived only as accumulator-level unit and proptest
cases — hand-written fixtures, never the sequences the 14 real adapters
actually emit (the PR's own stated deviation: start/end events are
internal, so the public drain can't observe them). Every fix round then
found another adapter that missed a shared rule by hand.

run_wire_stream and run_wire_buffered now run a SequenceLaws validator
over each interpret batch under cfg(any(test, debug_assertions)),
compiled out of release builds. Two laws — the obligation classes the
rounds kept re-finding:

- boundary: while a minted-key reasoning part is open, no text or tool
  content may be emitted; the adapter owns synthesizing the boundary
  end. Wire-keyed parts are exempt (Responses deliberately collapses
  across interleaving), as are whole-block Reasoning events (the mixed
  OpenRouter stream legally interleaves an encrypted block).
- intra-batch order: content-bearing events follow reasoning, text,
  tool-calls order within one frame batch; lifecycle bookkeeping (end
  events, terminals, ids, unknown passthrough) is exempt — closing an
  older entity after newer content is eviction, not disorder.

The check sits in the shared component every provider funnels through
(vercel's shared-accumulator rejections, pydantic-ai's
UnexpectedModelBehavior precedent), so every conformance fixture and
cassette replay now exercises the laws against real adapter output for
free. The full suite passes under it — the current adapters are clean,
and a future boundary-less wire that forgets its end fails loudly in
its own tests instead of surviving to a review round.

* refactor(streaming)!: the unknown payload Debug-redacts itself by type

The raw passthrough channel carried a bare serde_json::Value, so any
warn!(?value)-style Debug capture in a streaming module could leak wire
content — the class a four-round text scanner existed to police, each
round teaching it another Rust spelling it had missed.

RawStreamingChoice::Unknown, StreamedAssistantContent::Unknown, the
websocket Unknown variant, and the classify/triage internals now carry
streaming::UnknownPayload: #[serde(transparent)] (wire round-trips are
unchanged), redacted Debug (structural byte count only), and explicit
value()/into_value() accessors as the consumer opt-in. Debug-printing
the JSON channel now leaks nothing by construction — the redaction is a
property of the type, not a convention — with a unit pin asserting the
Debug output reproduces no payload content.

The warn-payload scan stays, with its scope narrowed and documented:
its remaining load-bearing target is payloads rig does not own the type
of (SDK frame enums, protos) whose derived Debug prints wire content —
the type system cannot withhold Debug on foreign types.

Follows the opaque-StreamPartId precedent from this same series:
41069f0ff made an observation class unrepresentable rather than tested.

* test(providers): name-keyed tool-result serializers carry a registry guard

The "read ToolResult::name, else pair from history" rule took four fix
commits because it lived as five hand-maintained serializer copies. All
five now route through the one shared resolver
(providers::internal::resolve_tool_result_names); this registry pins
that they keep doing so: each name-keyed wire's serializer source is
include_str!-compiled into the guard (moving the file breaks the build,
not just a scan — the compile-linked SUITE_FAMILIES precedent, #2258
F3) and must contain the resolver call.

Also documents why the chat-compat family stays a named skip for the
canonical interleaving scenario rather than gaining a fixture: probing
showed its buffered tool-call fragments only finalize at a wire-signaled
boundary, so AGGREGATED part order cannot pin reasoning→tool→reasoning
without risky early finalization — and the chat request format erases
part order on replay regardless (tool_calls is a flat array beside
content). The boundary the adapter does own — closing open reasoning
before tool content — is pinned at emission level by its unit tests and
the driver's debug-mode sequence laws.

* refactor(streaming): boundary-less adapters declare chunks; the lifecycle is derived once

The constant-key reasoning lifecycle — track reasoning_open, emit the
delta under the per-stream minted key, synthesize the silent boundary
end before any other content class, keep intra-chunk canonical order —
was hand-rolled in four adapters (ollama, cohere, gemini REST, gemini
interactions). It is the single largest source of fix-round findings:
the boundary rule alone took two rounds across the family, intra-chunk
order another, and each round found one more adapter that missed a
piece by hand.

Adapters now declare what one wire chunk carried (ChunkParts: reasoning,
an optional wire-carried signature close, text, prebuilt tool events)
and providers::internal::chunk_lifecycle::MintedReasoningLifecycle
derives the canonical sequence — reasoning delta, authoritative signed
close, synthesized boundary end when other content interleaves, text,
tool events. "Forgot the boundary" and "wrong intra-chunk order" are
not expressible through this interface (langchain's declarative-chunk +
core-side merge factoring; semantic-kernel converged on the same shape
independently), and the driver's debug-mode sequence laws still watch
the emitted stream, so bypassing the helper fails the adapter's own
tests.

Out of scope by design: wires that announce their own boundaries
(anthropic content_block_stop, Responses output_item.done) keep the
wire's lifecycle; the chat-completions compat family keeps its
CompatibleStreamProfile system, which already IS the shared derivation
for its ~15 gateway providers and models quirks (slot eviction,
encrypted reasoning details, decorations) this declarative shape does
not. The now-unused shared_parts reasoning helpers are deleted; the
gemini-grpc crate (typed transport, other crate) keeps its own emission
and remains pinned by its conformance suite and the sequence laws.

Adapter output is unchanged: the full suite, conformance scenarios, and
cassette replays pass byte-identical.

* refactor(streaming): shed caller-less identity surface; stale references swept

Post-review cleanup of the branch's own churn:
- SyntheticIds::block (zero callers, pre-existing) and ::reasoning (self-
  test only — constant-key wires mint via StreamPartId::minted directly)
  are gone; for_index is private (MintKind::for_wire_index is the public
  spelling).
- UnknownPayload::into_value had no caller; .value() and From cover use.
- The CHANGELOG no longer advertises an optimization to
  close_minted_reasoning, which this same release deletes, and gains the
  missing entries for the correlator-restatement and UnknownPayload
  breaking changes.
- A rig-agent comment referencing the deleted merge_reasoning_blocks
  states the rule directly; the chunk-lifecycle doc names all four
  converted wires; identity.rs drops the last 'composite' vocabulary.

* docs(streaming): public StreamPartId doc names wire_str as a code span

rustdoc -D warnings rejects a public doc linking the crate-private
accessor; the sentence keeps the reference without the intra-doc link.

* fix(streaming)!: sequence laws log always, panic only in rig's harness; whole blocks close their key; order law removed

Three defects in the round-4 sequence-law validator, found by adversarial
review of the guard itself:

- A same-key whole-block Reasoning event never cleared the open minted
  key, so ordinary Bedrock extended-thinking streams (deltas, then the
  full block at contentBlockStop, then text) and OpenAI Responses
  envelope-less replay bodies (id-less summary delta, done-item
  restatement under the adopted minted key, then text) tripped the
  boundary law. A whole block is open + restatement + close in ONE event
  (pydantic-ai's replace-part semantics; the Bedrock adapter's own
  'supersedes' contract) — it now closes the key, and both shapes are
  pinned by driver-routed regression tests.

- The intra-batch order law is deleted. Pass-through adapters forward
  provider parts in wire order and no wire contracts an order — every
  reference SDK iterates parts as delivered — so the law could fail on
  legal wire data (Gemini text-after-functionCall is the repo's own
  fixture shape). Canonical order is the chunk_lifecycle canonicalizer's
  property and is unit-tested there.

- panic! reached downstream applications: cargo compiles dependencies
  with debug-assertions in the dev profile, so a wrong law aborted user
  processes mid-stream. Violations now always emit
  tracing::error!(target: 'rig::sequence_law', ...) (variant names only)
  and panic only under cfg(any(test, feature = 'test-utils')). The new
  rig-core self-dev-dependency turns test-utils on for every rig-core
  test target via feature unification, and rig-bedrock's dev-deps enable
  it too — the laws still fail all of rig's own suites loudly while a
  downstream debug build gets a grep-able error log.

The guard's own coverage gap is the lesson: the one scenario that would
have caught this was a named skip for the affected provider, and the
adapters' tests bypassed the shared driver. The regression tests drive
the shared drivers.

* fix(streaming): a reused reasoning key's fresh part mints a fresh correlator

reasoning_start under a finished key correctly opened a NEW accumulator
part, but the stream handler installed no live correlator for it —
minting lived only in the delta arm. A part that then closed with no
deltas (a signature-only end) fell back to the finished-correlator map
and inherited the PREVIOUS part's public identity: two distinct
completed parts, one correlator, violating the one-correlator-per-part
contract (and priming the assembler to replace the earlier part once
same-correlator completions supersede).

reasoning_start now reports whether it genuinely opened a part (the
duplicate-start-on-open-key no-op returns false, preserving any live
correlator a prior delta installed), and the ReasoningStart arm mints a
fresh live correlator on a true open — pydantic-ai's stop-tracking
semantics: key reuse after close is a new identity, never the old
part's. The take-then-retain flow in reasoning_end_correlator is
untouched.

* fix(agent): a same-correlator completion replaces its part, never duplicates it

ingest_completed_reasoning matched the stream correlator only while a
part was Pending. The stream contract deliberately restates one
correlator per part — including on a late signature-bearing completion
after an unsigned close — so the second completion appended a duplicate
part (no provider id) or double-extended its own text through the
shared-provider-id fallback (with one).

An exact correlator match now identifies the part regardless of state
and replaces the slot wholesale (pydantic-ai's replace-part semantics;
the completed block always carries the whole content, the accumulator
having merged signatures before yielding), checked BEFORE the
provider-id fallbacks — which keep serving pending supersede and the
multi-part same-id extend for parts with different correlators. Both
probe shapes are ported as regression tests.

* fix(providers): id-less tool calls mint per-stream keys, never a shared constant

shared_parts::function_call keyed every id-less whole call with the
constant Minted(Tool, 0). The accumulator matches open assemblies by
exact key before its minted-vs-wire veto, so on the Interactions wire —
whose id-less step-0 assembly uses the same key — a whole call arriving
mid-assembly adopted and silently swallowed it: the model requested two
tools, the agent executed one, no error surfaced. Ollama's streaming
decode had the sibling defect: the per-record index enumeration handed
id-less calls in separate records the same Minted(Tool, 0).

Every id-less call now draws from a per-stream SyntheticIds::tool()
minter (the unanimous SDK pattern — vercel generates an id per id-less
call, pydantic-ai appends a new part per None vendor id, openai-agents
keys by distinct wire index; rig's own ToolCallBridge already holds a
per-stream minter). The Interactions adapter shares ONE minter between
its fragmenting step assemblies and its whole calls — drawing both from
one counter is what makes their keys disjoint — and the ollama adapter
counts across the stream, not per record. Durable ids stay absent for
id-less calls; only the opaque accumulation key changes.

* fix(agent): the invalid-call retry transcript mints its tool_call_id

The diagnostic call/result pair for an invalid streamed tool name went
onto the wire with an empty id: no serializer filters emptiness, Chat
Completions requires a non-empty tool_calls[].id, and two retries in
one conversation were indistinguishable.

The id is minted exactly at the transcript boundary
(rollback_messages), where the pair is rig-fabricated conversational
fiction and rig is the id's legitimate author — pydantic-ai's
generated-tool-call-id posture. Everything upstream stays faithful to
the wire: the in-memory diagnostic call, the invalid-call hooks, and
the consumer-visible synthetic result all still report that the
provider issued no id (correlation stays on internal_call_id), and
call_id stays None so no serializer mistakes the mint for a provider
handle.

* fix(agent): the skipped-tool map keys by position, not by tool-call id

On id-less wires (older ollama daemons) every call in a turn carries an
empty id, so the id-keyed skipped map collapsed: a second skipped call
overwrote the first, both read back one preresolved result, and a
non-skipped id-less call matched a skipped entry it never earned.

The map now keys by the call's position in the turn's items — the
openai-agents index-keyed pattern, and the disambiguator the code
already uses for internal-call-id pairing. Position is stable at every
site for free: the skip insert IS next_index, the peer fill enumerates,
the reader enumerates; the ignore-path removal only touches the current
slot, so earlier keys never shift. No id is fabricated at any decode
boundary. Regression: two id-less calls, one skipped — each reads its
own result.

* docs(streaming): UnknownPayload no longer splits RawStreamingChoice's doc

The struct was inserted mid-doc-comment: UnknownPayload's rendered docs
opened with 'Enum representing a streaming chunk from the model' ending
in a dangling comma, while the enum itself was documented only by the
orphaned tail fragment. Each item now owns its complete comment.

* refactor(message)!: tool-call identity is typed — ToolCallId + ProviderCallId

The message layer receives the identity decomposition the streaming layer
already has (StreamPartId vs WireId): rig's correlation handle and the
provider's wire handles are different types, and the empty-string tool-call
id sentinel is unrepresentable.

- ToolCall { id: ToolCallId, provider: Option<ProviderCallId> } replaces
  { id: String, call_id: Option<String> }; ToolResult { call, provider,
  name: String } replaces { id, call_id, name: Option<String> }.
- ToolCallId is non-empty by construction and minted at the provider
  boundary when the wire issued no id (from_wire / from_dual_wire), so
  every site that compares or keys by a tool-call id is correct on id-less
  wires (older Ollama daemons, Gemini REST, Vertex).
- Serializers send provider.call_id when the provider issued one, else the
  minted handle on wires that require an id; optional-id wires (Gemini
  REST/gRPC) omit minted handles entirely. The Interactions/Responses/xAI
  'requires call_id' request errors are unrepresentable and removed.
- resolve_tool_result_names (the 137-line legacy pairing shim) is deleted
  with its name-in-id encodings; ToolResult::name is required and read
  directly by all four name-keyed serializers. The name-keyed-serializer
  meta-test pins the successor contract.
- Hooks and telemetry surface the durable id (provider's, else minted) —
  never Some("").
- Persisted-history serde is breaking; MIGRATING.md documents the change.

Dissolves review items 2 (retry feedback collapsing onto every id-less
peer), 8 (hook contexts carrying Some("")), and 9 (peers keeping "" in
the fabricated retry transcript), and answers item 7's Interactions
call_id requirement in the type system.

* fix(providers): a multi-block reasoning done item aggregates as one part

OpenAI Responses (and xai, which shares the adapter) emitted a separate
whole-block choice per summary entry, per content entry, and one more for
encrypted_content — all under one key and one rs_* provider id. The
accumulator turns every restatement after the first into a new sibling
part, so a turn configured with reasoning summaries plus
include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"] replayed two (or more) reasoning
input items carrying the identical rs_* id on the next request.

Fix at the adapter, where every inspected SDK guarantees one reasoning
input item per rs_* id on replay: the done item now emits ONE wire-sent
ReasoningEnd restatement carrying every block in wire field order
(summary, content, encrypted), so reasoning_end supersedes the delta-built
part in place and history replays exactly one rs_* input item. An empty
done item emits nothing, as before.

The debug sequence law already treats ReasoningEnd as the part's close, so
the envelope-less minted-key shape stays covered. Tests pinning the old
per-block emission are rewritten to pin the fused shape, and the
encrypted-reasoning cassette test now asserts the one-part aggregation
outright — the regression test this class was missing.

* fix(streaming): a second signature records a distinct part, never an overwrite

Every boundary-less wire keys reasoning by one per-stream constant
(Minted(Reasoning, 0) — gemini REST and Interactions via
shared_parts::REASONING_ID, cohere, ollama), so a signature-only
ReasoningEnd for the already-finished key hit attach_reasoning_signature's
last-text-slot write and OVERWROTE the previously recorded signature: two
signed segments in one turn left only the last signature in history — the
MISSING_THOUGHT_SIGNATURE replay failure this branch set out to close.

Signatures cannot merge (Google's doctrine: don't combine two parts that
both carry signatures), so:
- attach_reasoning_signature targets the last UNSIGNED text slot, keeping
  the push fallback when no unsigned slot exists;
- the finished-key signature-only arm of reasoning_end pushes a distinct
  sibling reasoning part (the shape the never-seen-key branch already
  builds) and repoints the key when the finished part is already signed.

Regression test drives the exact constant-key double-signature sequence:
before the fix it yields one part [("thought A", sig_B)]; now both
signatures survive, each on its own part.

* fix(providers): Interactions closes open assemblies at interaction.completed

step.start only opens an assembly and the completed call existed solely
because step.stop pushed ToolInputEnd; interaction.completed pushed the
terminal record and the driver returned without finish (which is empty),
so PartsAccumulator::finish cleared the still-open input. A step.stop
that was missing, late, or reordered therefore lost the whole call: the
consumer saw name/args deltas but no ToolCall, and the agent treated a
tool-calling turn as plain text.

The interaction.completed arm now synthesizes ToolInputEnd for each entry
still in open_function_steps (announcement order) before the terminal
record: this event is the provider's own proof the turn finished, so a
still-open step means a lost close frame, not truncation. The accumulator
finalizes the call from its accumulated fragments under the step's
existing Error policy.

Deliberately NOT taken: draining open_tool_inputs in the shared
PartsAccumulator::finish. That path is the settled truncation contract
(calls still open at transport EOF never fully arrived and drop); a
blanket drain would turn genuinely truncated partial JSON into policy
errors. The adapter-level close covers exactly the known-complete case
and leaves truncation semantics untouched.

Regression test: step.start + arguments_delta + interaction.completed
with no step.stop must yield the completed call with its streamed
arguments and the terminal record.

* fix(streaming): whole-call adoption demands restatement evidence, not cardinality

tool_call's fallback adopted 'the single open minted assembly' whenever
the incoming whole-call key was wire-derived — the assembly's name and
buffer were never consulted. Gemini Interactions emits both fragmenting
assemblies (step.start + arguments_delta) and whole calls (step.delta
function_call): an unrelated id-bearing whole call arriving while an
id-less assembly was open removed that assembly, marked it finished, and
stole its internal_call_id; the assembly's own step.stop then finalized
nothing and its streamed arguments were silently lost.

Adoption now requires the whole call to actually restate the assembly:
the tool name must match, and the call's arguments must cover whatever
fragments streamed (none at all, or a lenient parse the arguments
subsume). Otherwise the whole call appends as its own part and the
assembly stays open for its own end — the legitimate late-wire-key
restatement is preserved, and an unrelated call can no longer steal
streamed arguments. This is the surviving half of review O3; the
constant-key half landed in 4be803ca.

Regression tests: a different-tool call and a same-tool call with
contradicting arguments both leave the assembly to finalize itself; the
legitimate-restatement pin now restates matching arguments.

* fix(providers): Interactions announce arguments are replace-if-no-deltas

A step.start carrying non-empty arguments pushed them as a raw fragment,
and later arguments_delta fragments appended to the same buffer with no
reconciliation — {"x":1}{"x":1} — so under the step's Error policy the
accumulator returned ResponseError and the call was lost. The {}-only
guard covered the recorded shape but not a partial announce (the
adapter's own doc says the start 'usually' carries {}), and a non-object
announce value slipped through the same push.

The announce payload is no longer a fragment: it is recorded on the open
step and used only when no arguments_delta ever arrives. Fragments, when
they arrive, ARE the arguments. Both step.stop and the
interaction.completed orphan-close route go through one helper, so the
fallback applies on either close path.

Regression tests: announce {"x":1} + delta {"x":1} + stop must yield
the call with {"x":1} (was ResponseError); announce-only with no
fragments still finalizes from the announce payload.

* fix(bedrock): foreign encrypted reasoning degrades, never ships as redactedContent

ReasoningContent::Encrypted was bucketed with Bedrock-native Redacted:
an all-encrypted foreign block (OpenAI Responses encrypted_content,
OpenRouter reasoning.encrypted, Anthropic — all stored verbatim, never
base64) reached BASE64_STANDARD.decode. An unpadded/URL-safe token failed
the whole request locally with a misleading 'not valid base64' error, and
one that happened to decode shipped another provider's ciphertext to
Converse as Bedrock's own redactedContent — contradicting the
degrade-don't-fail policy the same function states for the mixed case.

Provenance is in the variant: only Redacted (base64 applied by this
file's own inbound legs) may decode back onto the wire. Encrypted is
always foreign at this serializer and now warns + drops in every position,
including the all-encrypted block, which degrades away entirely (the
outbound conversion gained an Ok(None) channel for blocks Converse cannot
carry). A native Redacted blob that no longer decodes also warns + drops
instead of failing the request, consistent with the mixed-block policy.

The old test pinning Encrypted→decode→RedactedContent is rewritten to pin
the drop; new tests pin the never-fails and never-ships properties for
the verbatim token shapes foreign producers actually store.

* fix(providers): Responses reasoning keys are slot-scoped, not per-event

The reasoning accumulation key came from each frame's own item_id while
the tool path deliberately resolves through a slot-scoped ToolCallBridge:
gateways and ChatGPT's envelope-less replay bodies omit the id on a
subset of a slot's events, so a slot mixing id-bearing and id-less
frames split into Wire("rs_1") and Minted(Output, i). The done item
resolved through the minted-only map and superseded just one half — the
other survived as an orphaned partial part carrying the same provider
id, compounding the duplicate-input-item class.

Reasoning now gets the ToolCallBridge treatment: reasoning_slots fixes
one assembly key per output slot at the slot's first reasoning event
(wire id when present, else minted output-{index}); every later frame
reuses the stored key regardless of the id it carries, and the done item
resolves through the slot map (a slot with no established identity keeps
the wire id — the pure-replay shape). The per-event closure and the
minted-only minted_reasoning_ids map it subsumes are gone. A late wire id
still upgrades the part's durable provider_id as data, never the key.

Regression test drives the mixed slot end to end: one assembly key
across all frames, one aggregated reasoning part.

* fix(providers): an unparseable restatement is not re-emitted over streamed fragments

When the restated output_item.done function-call arguments failed to
parse, the raw string was re-emitted as a ToolCallDelta::Delta
unconditionally — including when function_call_arguments.delta frames had
already streamed those exact bytes (the max_output_tokens-mid-tool-call
shape). The assembly buffer held the partial JSON twice, a consumer
reassembling deltas rendered it twice, and the bytes were double-charged
against the accumulation bound.

ToolCallSlot gains saw_arguments_delta (set in the args-delta arm;
ToolCallBridge::open now returns &mut so the arm can mark it). The Err
arm re-emits the raw restatement only when NO fragment preceded the done
item — the pure-replay / truncated-restatement case, where the bytes
must still reach the buffer so the settled truncation policy (#2258 P3)
has something to judge.

Regression tests pin both halves: fragments seen → the buffer holds the
bytes once; a fragment-less truncated restatement still routes its raw
string through the buffer.

* fix(providers): a model_output step yields every convertible item

step_start_to_choice ran find_map over the step's content, so a
model_output step interleaving text and a function_call kept only the
first convertible item — a call following text in the same step silently
vanished (the #[serde(default)] content from #2258 makes content-bearing
step.start frames a modeled shape, so the path is reachable). The
conversion now collects all convertible items in wire order and the
StepStart arm emits each; the unary content_to_choice recursion keeps its
0-or-1 shape via into_iter().next().

Regression test: same-step text-then-function_call yields both.

* docs(changelog): describe the shipped surface, not the phases that led to it

Both unreleased entry sets ship in one release, so a reader following
them writes against removed APIs:

- rig-agent still claimed MultiTurnStreamItem delta ids render minted
  identities namespaced (rig:reasoning:0) and that id-less calls carry
  the absent (empty) durable id — phase B removed the rendering,
  ToolCallDelta has no id field, and the empty sentinel is now
  unrepresentable. The entry now states the final correlator surface and
  the typed tool-call identity hooks observe.
- rig-core still described streaming::PartId, a ReasoningSignature
  variant, and a (item id, part ordinal)-keyed accumulator; none exist
  at head. Collapsed to the shipped design (opaque StreamPartId keys,
  signature-bearing ReasoningEnd, the lifecycle-event accumulator), and
  the resolve_tool_result_names / name: Option entries are rewritten for
  the typed ToolCallId + ProviderCallId model that replaced them.
- Added Fixed entries for this round's streaming/provider fixes and
  bedrock's foreign-ciphertext degrade.

Tool identity holds at every boundary: legacy lift, honest constructors, and the drains the siblings already had (2262 round-7 follow-up) (#2267)

* refactor(message): single-source the wire-id and correlation-handle derivations

Every required-id wire re-derived "provider call_id else minted handle"
by hand — 13 identical copies across seven provider serializers — and
the correlation-handle derivation was copy-pasted at six more sites.
Hand-rolled policy drifts (Bedrock's assistant leg already had).

ToolCall::wire_call_id()/ToolResult::wire_call_id() now encode the
required-id-wire policy next to from_wire (its inverse), and
ToolCallId::for_provider() is the one derivation both the message and
streaming layers share. Optional-id wires (Gemini REST, gRPC) keep
reading `provider` directly — minted handles never travel upstream
there.

* fix(bedrock): the assistant toolUse echo agrees with the result leg

assistant_content.rs sent the bare correlation handle as toolUseId
while user_content.rs sent the provider-issued call id when one exists
— the only provider whose two tool legs disagreed. A history whose
handle and provider id diverge (JSON-restored cross-provider
transcripts; ToolCall::new().with_provider()) replayed as
toolUse.toolUseId=minted vs toolResult.toolUseId=provider, which
Converse rejects as a tool result without matching toolUse.

Both legs now derive the id through wire_call_id().

* fix(message): legacy ToolCall JSON lifts call_id into provider, never drops it

Old payloads always wrote the `call_id` key (it was never skipped), so
its presence identifies the pre-provider-split schema. The derived
Deserialize treated it as an unknown key and discarded it silently: a
persisted Responses history loaded with provider:None and replayed the
fc_ item handle in the call_id slot, mispairing every
function_call_output — and MIGRATING.md's claim that old histories fail
loudly was false for ToolCall-bearing histories.

ToolCall now deserializes through a wire struct that lifts the legacy
key: dual-identifier payloads keep the correlator and the item handle,
single-identifier payloads keep the provider-supplied id as
provider.call_id (that is what the old field was documented to be), and
the current schema — no call_id key — is untouched, so minted handles
are never promoted.

* fix(message): a bare tool_result() string is the correlation handle, never a provider id

UserContent::tool_result stamped any non-empty string as a
provider-issued ProviderCallId. The natural echo pattern —
tool_result(&call.tool_call.id, …) after an id-less Gemini call —
laundered the minted handle into provider identity, and Gemini
serialization then emitted functionResponse.id=Some(minted) against a
functionCall that omitted its id: an asymmetric pair the API rejects,
and a direct violation of "minted handles never travel upstream" on
optional-id wires.

A bare string cannot prove provider provenance, so the constructor now
records it as the handle only. Wire output on required-id wires is
byte-identical (wire_call_id falls back to the handle). Call sites that
DO hold a wire-issued id — the inbound converters — move to the new
tool_result_from_wire(), the ToolResult mirror of ToolCall::from_wire;
driver code keeps tool_result_for.

* fix(interactions): a single-wire id travels as tool_id only

function_step_end filled both ToolInputEnd id slots with the one
identifier Interactions issues, so the shared accumulator took the
dual-wire arm and stored ProviderCallId{call_id: fc_X, item_id:
Some(fc_X)} — a fabricated Responses-shaped identity contradicting the
documented single-wire contract, and one whose fc_-prefixed fake item
id passes the Responses foreign-id guard on cross-provider replay.

The unary path already stamped item_id: None via from_wire; the
streamed path now matches. (tool_id, not call_id: the accumulator falls
back to the wire-derived assembly key for tool_id, so a call_id-only
emitter would still take the dual arm.)

* fix(streaming): adoption accepts nameless assemblies and the null placeholder

Two gateway fragment shapes the pre-lifecycle code adopted were
rejected by the whole-call adoption predicate, publishing the call
under a fresh minted id (breaking delta correlation) and finalizing the
open assembly as a duplicate:

- args-only fragmentation: an assembly opened by tool_args_delta never
  saw a name (ensure_open_tool_input records ""), and the predicate
  demanded exact name equality. An empty name is no evidence against
  the restatement — only a different established name vetoes.
- the literal `null` placeholder: parse yields Value::Null and strict
  subset comparison rejected it, even though tool_args_delta itself
  documents the placeholder as a real gateway shape. A buffer that
  streamed no real arguments is covered vacuously.

* fix(responses): a provider-completed call survives a lost output_item.done

A slot opened by output_item.added (or an arguments delta) closed only
via output_item.done; when that one frame was lost or undecodable, a
healthy response.completed still left the slot open and the shared
accumulator discarded the streamed call as truncation. The PR shipped
this exact terminal-proof drain in both sibling adapters (Interactions
at interaction.completed, chat-compat at finish_reason) — Responses now
matches: the terminal closes every open slot and the call finalizes
from its streamed fragments (parse-or-drop, so the truncation contract
for genuinely partial arguments is unchanged, as is bare-EOF handling).

Drained slots keep the full dual-wire identity: the call_id announced
at output_item.added rides a pending map beside the bridge (the bridge
gains drain_ordered_indexed so per-slot adapter state can rejoin its
slot at flush).

* fix(providers): name-keyed wires resolve an ingested result's empty name from its call

Rig's own inbound converters stamp ToolResult.name: "" — the
Anthropic, OpenAI-chat, Cohere, and Bedrock tool-result wires carry no
name — and every name-keyed serializer passed it through unfiltered, so
a cross-provider ingested transcript replayed to Gemini or Vertex sent
functionResponse.name: "" and got INVALID_ARGUMENT. Strictly worse
than the pre-2262 shim, which at least sent something non-empty.

The name lives on the result's paired call in the same history, so
name-keyed request assembly (Gemini REST, Interactions, Ollama, Vertex
AI, gemini-grpc) now fills empty names through
resolve_empty_tool_result_names — the typed-id descendant of the
deleted resolve_tool_result_names shim: matched by rig's correlation
handle, then provider identifiers; established names are never
overwritten; nothing pairs by position or name; an unmatched result
keeps its empty name (the transcript genuinely lacks the data).

* refactor(interactions): the step assembly is the shared ToolCallBridge

OpenFunctionStep{key, wire_id, saw_arguments_delta} re-implemented
ToolCallSlot — including the saw_arguments_delta field this same
release added to the shared slot for the Responses adapter — and the
interaction.completed flush was a byte-for-byte copy of
drain_ordered's body. Replace-if-no-deltas now lives in ONE place:
the slot's end_event applies the announce-payload fallback (the only
genuinely Interactions-specific piece, moved onto the shared slot as
announce_arguments), and the bridge's minter doubles as the whole-call
minter (minted_ids) so both id-less paths keep drawing from one
counter — the disjoint-keys invariant the hand-rolled version
maintained by convention.

refactor!: `OneOrMany<T>` becomes `Vec<T>` — the fake is deleted, the enforcement moves (#2273)

* refactor!: message content is Vec, not OneOrMany

`OneOrMany<T>` promised "at least one item" on a path where zero items is a
real outcome, so the code fabricated data to keep the promise. The type is
deleted; every list is a `Vec`.

Two facts carry this, both load-bearing rather than stylistic:

`is_empty()` returned a hardcoded `false`. Every caller asking a list whether
it was empty got the wrong answer with no compile error. Deleting the method
surfaced two live defects: mira's "Response contained empty content" was
unreachable, so a defective response surfaced as an empty completion instead of
an error; and an ollama test asserting `!choice.is_empty()` was asserting
`!false` and proving nothing.

The invariant it asserted was false. Seven production sites pushed an
`AssistantContent::text("")` the model never produced, purely so a content-less
turn could be represented — agent/run, prompt_request/streaming, candle's
parser, anthropic's `end_turn` branch, the streaming accumulator's initial state
and its `finish()`. A tool-call-only turn, a content-filtered turn, a truncated
stream and a local model emitting EOS immediately are all real; the fabricated
part reached history and the wire indistinguishable from a real empty text
block. `is_empty_assistant_turn` recognises both the honest empty turn and the
legacy sentinel, so histories persisted before this change keep round-tripping.

Removing the padding made three guards reachable that had never fired. Two
cancelled the run ("model turn lost its assistant content", "model-turn retry
lost the rejected assistant content") and one failed a local generation; all
three would have broken runs that previously succeeded, so all three are
removed. An empty assistant turn is legal, and the code immediately below each
of them already handled it.

Where the container was enforcing something real, the enforcement moved and
split by direction rather than vanishing:

- Outbound, once, at the request boundary: `validate_message_content` rejects an
  empty `chat_history` — non-empty by construction until now, and the field is
  public — and any user or assistant message with no content, naming the role
  and index instead of becoming a provider 400. System content is exempt: it is
  a `String` and the container never constrained it, so checking it would be a
  new restriction that breaks a conditionally built preamble resolving to "".
- Per wire, at each conversion: 25 sites route through
  `message::require_non_empty(items, || error)`, each keeping its own error text
  rather than borrowing the constructor's context-free "cannot create with an
  empty vector". Most are inbound — `normalize` and `TryFrom<ProviderResponse>`
  — where the claim is "this provider returned nothing where its protocol
  promises content", a provider defect and a different claim from "empty
  assistant content is illegal", which is exactly what was untrue. The rest sit
  in message serializers, where a content-less block has nothing to send.

The serialized form is unchanged, so persisted histories and stored embeddings
need no migration and **no recorded fixture changes**. The container already
wrote a plain sequence; its `Deserialize` implemented only `visit_seq` and
rejected `[]`, and that empty array is the single input whose behaviour differs
— it was an error and is now an empty list. `string_or_one_or_many` folds into
the existing `json_utils::string_or_vec`, which the two differed from only in
which list type they produced.

Three conversions could not remain trait impls: with both sides foreign, `impl
TryFrom<Vec<..>> for Vec<..>` violates the orphan rule. They are `pub` free
functions — `user_content_to_messages`, `assistant_content_to_messages`,
`reasoning_summaries` — so the change does not quietly narrow the public API.

Nine new tests cover what is new: the request-boundary rules including the
System exemption and the legacy sentinel still validating, and the serde
contract that makes the zero-fixture-churn claim checkable. 3547 pass, clippy
`-D warnings` and fmt clean, 132 doctests, zero cassette diffs, and no
`OneOrMany` left in any `.rs` outside two comments explaining why two functions
are free functions.

* fix: finish the fabrication removal and close the validation gap

A comparison review against the parallel #2272 found four places where this
branch claimed more than it delivered, plus two cleanups that PR got right.

**Two fabricated empty-text parts survived a claim they were gone.** The
migration commit said seven production sites, and removed five. Anthropic's
documented empty `end_turn` still normalized a content-less turn into
`vec![text("")]`, and the run loop still padded `resolving.items` after dropping
its last entry. Both are removed, so an empty turn is empty on every path
instead of most of them; the streaming assembler's initial `last_final_choice`
goes with them. The count was also wrong: six sites fabricated to satisfy the
container, not seven. The seventh `text("")` — `ensure_text_block` — is a slot
that deltas fill and `finish` drops if nothing arrives, so it stays, and the
guide now says why. The stale comment above the anthropic site, still asserting
that the response type "requires at least one assistant item", is gone with it.

Anthropic's empty `end_turn` is pinned by a unit test and a cassette test; both
now assert an empty choice. The recorded provider bodies are untouched — what
changed is rig's spelling of the same response, which is the whole point.

**`validate_message_content` was not wired into the path that carries most
traffic.** It ran in `CompletionRequestBuilder::send`/`stream` only; the agent
loop builds its request directly and calls `ModelHandle::completion`/`stream`,
so every agent-driven request went unchecked — including the empty
`chat_history` this validation exists to catch. `ModelHandle` now validates at
both entry points, and the doc says exactly which paths are covered and which
are not, instead of claiming "before the network".

**Decoding widened in two places, and only one was documented.** The guide said
the empty array was "the one input that behaved differently". It is not:
`json_utils::string_or_vec` carries `visit_none`/`visit_unit`, so the fields
that moved onto it now accept `null` where they used to raise a parse error.
Those arms cannot be dropped — the OpenAI assistant-content field that already
used this helper depends on them, because OpenAI sends `"content": null` for a
tool-calls-only message. Documented, and pinned by four tests over the helper's
string / sequence / `[]` / `null` arms, which nothing covered before.

**A tool with `Output = Vec<ToolResultContent>` changes wire payload with no
compile error.** `IntoToolOutput`'s rich-content guard used to name
`OneOrMany<ToolResultContent>`; naming `Vec` means such a tool stops falling
through to `Serialize` as one JSON array and starts sending N ordered content
blocks, with images as image parts. That is what the guard always intended, and
for nearly every tool it is the wanted result, but a prompt parsing that JSON
array needs updating — so it gets its own section rather than shipping silent.
The empty-vec case (`content: []` where it was `json([])`) is called out too.

Also: `merge`'s row in the migration table now says the `?` rejection is lost
rather than only showing the replacement; a dead `unwrap_or_else` fallback after
`chat_history.push(prompt)` is deleted, along with the clone it forced; the
streaming driver's "`finish` is never empty" comment described the invariant
this PR removed; and the two extracted OpenAI conversions lose the vestigial
brace block left from unwrapping their old impl bodies.

3551 pass (+4), 132 doctests, clippy `-D warnings` and fmt clean, zero cassette
diffs.

* fix: retract two false claims and the redundant check one of them justified

Cross-review of #2272 found three documentation-integrity defects here, one of
which I had made worse rather than better.

**The mira claim is false, and the last commit promoted it to a release note.**
I said `"Response contained empty content"` was dead code behind the container's
hardcoded-`false` `is_empty()` and became reachable when content became a `Vec`.
The predicate was never what kept it dead: `TryFrom<RawMessage>` builds the
assistant arm as `vec![AssistantContent::Text(..)]` unconditionally
(`providers/mira.rs:169`), so the list holds exactly one element even when the
wire sent an empty string. The guard was unreachable before this migration and
is unreachable after it. The `*(mira)* [**behavior**]` CHANGELOG bullet
announcing a change that does not happen is deleted, the MIGRATING paragraph
with it, and the guard now carries a comment saying why it cannot fire — so the
next reader does not repeat the deduction I got wrong.

This also retracts a claim made against #2272 during review: its "provider
behavior does not change" statement is correct on mira, and mine was the false
one.

**`ModelHandle` validation was justified by a false premise, so it goes.** The
rationale said the agent loop bypasses `CompletionRequestBuilder`. It does not:
the blocking turn issues `prepared.builder.send()` (`runner.rs:930`) and the
streaming turn `prepared.builder.stream()`, and the builder already validates.
The check therefore ran twice on every agent request, scanning the whole history
each time, to close a gap that was never open. Reverted; the builder is the
request boundary, and `ModelHandle` now documents that it deliberately adds no
validation of its own. `validate_message_content`'s own doc, MIGRATING and the
CHANGELOG all said "does not go through the builder" in some form; all three now
describe what actually happens.

fix(anthropic): prefer `message_delta` usage.input_tokens when the provider sends it there (#2279)

* fix(anthropic): prefer message_delta usage.input_tokens when the provider sends it there

The streaming adapter captured `input_tokens` at `message_start` and
discarded the terminal `message_delta`'s own value, even though
`PartialUsage` already models the field.

Anthropic proper reports the prompt size on `message_start` and omits it
from `message_delta`, so this was correct against the real API. But
Anthropic-compatible gateways do not all agree: OpenRouter's Messages
endpoint sends `input_tokens: 0` on `message_start` and the real count on
`message_delta`, so consumers silently saw `Usage { input_tokens: 0 }` —
worse than a missing value for anything sizing a context window from it.

Prefer the delta and fall back to `message_start`. A zero on the delta is
treated as "not reported" rather than as a count, so a gateway with the
inverse split cannot erase a prompt size `message_start` reported
correctly. Behaviour against Anthropic proper is unchanged.

fix(gemini): send temperature and max_tokens; add live regression cassettes and a cache-prefix guard (#2283)

* test(providers): live regression cassettes, and fix Gemini dropping temperature/max_tokens

Adds the first tranche of a live-recorded regression suite (proposal:
many_rigs/rig-regression-cassette-suite-proposal.md) covering shipped fixes
whose *premise* was never recorded, and fixes the bug the first recording
session found.

## The bug

`gemini::completion::create_request_body` applied `temperature` and
`max_tokens` through `generation_config.map(...)`. `Option::map` is a no-op on
`None`, so a request that set either field without ALSO supplying an
`additional_params.generationConfig` dropped both silently: `.max_tokens(8)` on
a Gemini agent never reached `maxOutputTokens`, and `.temperature(0.0)` never
reached the wire.

Found by recording a cassette that asserted a `max_tokens(8)` turn reports
`FinishReason::Length`; it reported `Stop`. The mapping and the normalization
were both correct, so querying Gemini directly settled it — the wire does send
`"finishReason": "MAX_TOKENS"` for `maxOutputTokens: 8`. rig had never sent the
field.

It survived because every pre-existing Gemini cassette passes an
`additional_params` `GenerationConfig` for `thinkingConfig`, which makes the
Option `Some` and the `map` fire. The whole corpus shared one usage pattern
that dodges the defect; nothing exercised the plain agent-builder path.

The config is now created when either field is set, mirroring the
`output_schema` arm above it, and seeded with both fields cleared rather than
`GenerationConfig::default()` (temperature 1.0 / maxOutputTokens 4096) so
setting one field does not silently send the other.

## Blast radius

62 of 127 committed Gemini cassettes had recorded the bug — their request
bodies say `"generationConfig":null` where the caller set `.temperature(0.0)`.
Those tool-calling tests pinned temperature 0 for determinism and were in fact
recorded at Gemini's default temperature. All re-recorded live.

`document_ordering` then failed on its own `max_tokens(32)`, which only ever
passed while the bound was being discarded; raised to 512 with the reason
recorded, since that test is about document ordering, not truncation.

## Cassettes

Recorded live across all three providers:

- anthropic `streaming/input_tokens_agree_across_frames` — pins the premise
  #2279's comment rests on (both frames carry input_tokens and agree), which
  the existing cassettes only satisfied incidentally
- anthropic `regression/stop_reason_{max_tokens,end_turn}` — the other half of
  issue #2235, plus its counterpart so `Length` is proven specific to truncation
- openai `regression/chat_compat_finish_reason{,_natural}` — issue #2248
- gemini `regression/agent_max_tokens_without_additional_params` — pins the fix
  above; the recorded request body is the assertion, per tests/README.md's
  "assert on the request boundary too"

## Known failure

`hook_stress::request_patch_injects_context_and_narrows_active_tools_blocking`
is red (gemini 168/169; anthropic 116/116, openai 146/146). Its hook pins
temperature 0.0, which until this fix never reached Gemini; at a genuine 0 the
model answers only the arithmetic half of the prompt and the injected-context
assertion fails. The test is byte-identical to main — a speculative prompt
rewrite was tried, did not help, and was reverted rather than weakening the
assertion. Diagnosis and next step are recorded as B-7 in the proposal.

* test(gemini): resolve the hook_stress context-injection failure at temperature 0

The last red test from the previous commit. Its hook pins `.temperature(0.0)`,
which never reached Gemini until the `create_request_body` fix, so it had
recorded at the default 1.0. At a genuine 0 the model answered only the
arithmetic half and the injected-context assertion failed.

Diagnosed rather than patched around; each step killed a hypothesis:

1. Is the injected context reaching the model? Decoded every recorded request
   body — the vault document is present on both real completion calls (turn 1
   and the post-tool turn). The hook rides every turn as designed. Not a hook
   bug.
2. Is Gemini declining to echo something framed as a credential? Probed the
   live wire at temperature 0 with the fact framed as "the vault access code"
   and as a neutral "inventory reference token". Both echoed it back. Not a
   refusal.
3. Is it the tool loop? The model returned "42", then "SUM: 42" under an
   explicit two-line format — following the format for the arithmetic line and
   dropping the other. It omits the *first* requested item when a tool call
   intervenes.

Fix: ask for the tool result first and the context-derived code second, both
stated as required. The assertion is unchanged; only prompt ordering moved, and
the reason is recorded at the call site.

The general rule now documented in the proposal: at a genuine temperature 0, a
multi-part prompt whose first item is not the tool call loses that item. Put the
tool-dependent line first in any cassette asserting on both.

gemini 169/169, anthropic 116/116, openai 146/146.

* test(cassettes): guard recorded conversations against moving their cache prefix

Task 2 of the remaining-work plan. Ports the strongest idea from
`inspirations/pydantic-ai` (`tests/cassette_utils.py`
`check_cache_prefix_stability`), which guards this across a 1313-cassette
corpus. The invariant is imported; the plumbing is rig's.

Provider prompt caching is a prefix match: the cache key derives from the exact
bytes up to each breakpoint, so a turn that rewrites, reorders, or drops a block
an earlier turn already sent busts the cache on every subsequent turn. Nothing
pinned that. Each cassette test asserts on its own turn's values; none compared
turn N-1's request against turn N's. The check is derived entirely from
cassettes already recorded — no provider traffic, and it applies retroactively
to all 500+ fixtures.

Three refinements were needed to make it precise, each from a false positive the
first run surfaced:

1. Consecutive same-endpoint requests are not necessarily one conversation.
   Batch extractors and document tests record several independent single-turn
   requests per cassette. Identity is now the first message-level block.
2. On OpenAI-compatible wires the system prompt is itself a `messages` entry and
   is identical across unrelated runs sharing a preamble, so identity skips
   system/developer roles and keys on the conversation's opening turn.
3. An independent repeat re-sends the same opening turn with a different tool
   schema. A real continuation *grew*, so a pair is only compared when the later
   request has more message blocks than the earlier.

A single-object field (Anthropic's string `system`, Gemini's `systemInstruction`
Content object) is treated as one block rather than iterated — iterating would
reduce it to its keys and blind the check to content changes. pydantic-ai
documents hitting exactly that; a unit test pins it here.

Result: 4 exemptions, each with a written reason, and no rig defect. Two are a
hook whose whole purpose is rewriting the request; two are hand-built follow-up
requests in streaming_grammar that intentionally omit `.tool(...)`. Verified
that the production path is clean — the agent loop re-advertises the full tool
set on every turn (multi_turn_streaming_tools: 4 turns, 4 identical tool lists).

Also settles task 2a: no work needed. rig's harness already fails the
zero-interactions-played case (`assert_replay_finished` treats every unconsumed
interaction as a failure), so it is already at the setting pydantic-ai exposes
as opt-in `--strict-vcr-cassette-usage`. Confirmed empirically with a throwaway
probe before deleting it.

* test(anthropic): record the cache-hit accounting the `> 0` filter depends on (A5)

Task 3. `anthropic/streaming.rs` filters the terminal `message_delta`'s
`input_tokens` with `> 0` and documents that as a *heuristic, not an invariant*:
with prompt caching, a turn whose prefix is cached bills few or zero uncached
input tokens while the real prompt size sits in `cache_read_input_tokens`. The
comment then warns against extending the filter to `message_start` or the cache
fields, where a genuine zero would be discarded. Nothing pinned that semantic.

The recording states it in numbers: on the cache-hit turn Anthropic reports

    cache_read_input_tokens: 4512
    input_tokens: 3

for a ~4515-token prompt. `input_tokens` is the uncached remainder, not the
prompt size — precisely the premise the filter rests on.

Asserts the relationship (cached dominates the remainder) rather than a literal.
The catalogue predicted this turn might report exactly 0; it reported 3, so a
literal assertion would have been wrong and a re-record could turn one into a
tautology either way.

Group A is otherwise already covered, found by grepping before writing as the
plan requires: parallel-tool distinctness lives in streaming_grammar, the empty
end-turn in empty_end_turn.rs, signature/thinking replay in opus_4_7.rs and
reasoning_tool_roundtrip.rs. The three negative paths (A8 malformed
content_block_delta, A9 unknown event, A12 non-object frame) cannot be elicited
from a live provider and are already spelled in the streaming conformance corpus
as `malformed_frame` and `unknown_event_frame` — the mechanism built for exactly
that, per tests/README.md.

ci: pin sccache and make its install best-effort (#2292)

The `test guards` job on main failed with two errors that both trace back
to `mozilla/sccache-action` rather than to anything rig compiles:

    HttpError: self-signed certificate
    Unable to locate executable file: undefined

With no `version` input the action resolves the release through a
`repos.getLatestRelease` API call on every run; a runner's egress proxy
served a self-signed certificate and the call — and with it the whole
job — died before a single crate was compiled. The second error is the
action's post step, which is not optional and shells out to
`$SCCACHE_PATH --show-stats` even when the install never happened.

Pin the version so the API call disappears (it also stops CI silently
tracking whatever sccache released today), set `disable_annotations` so
the post step returns before it can fail on an unset path, and mark the
install `continue-on-error` with the `RUSTC_WRAPPER` export gated on its
outcome. A failed download now costs a slower compile instead of a red
run, and RUSTC_WRAPPER never points at a binary that is not there.

* fix(openai): preserve Responses message phase across stateless replay (#2269)

gpt-5.6-era models stamp a `phase` (e.g. final_answer) on message output
items, and OpenAI documents that follow-up requests should replay it —
dropping it can degrade performance. OutputMessage silently dropped the
field at deserialization, so every replayed history omitted it (visible
in all committed multi-turn gpt-5.6 cassettes: phase in each response,
absent from each follow-up request).

The field now survives end to end: OutputMessage carries it (raw-path
serialization stays value-equal), ingest parks it in the first text
block's wire extras (the same vehicle as annotations), and request
assembly hoists it back to the message level, where the recorded live
traffic shows OpenAI accepting it.

feat(venice): add Venice AI provider with live-recorded cassette coverage (#2306)

* feat(venice): add Venice AI provider

New `providers::venice` for the Venice API (https://docs.venice.ai),
covering every capability Rig has a trait for:

- completions and streaming through the shared OpenAI-compatible
  `GenericCompletionModel` (tools, vision, structured output, reasoning);
- embeddings via the shared OpenAI-compatible embeddings path (Venice
  honors `dimensions` and `encoding_format`);
- `GET /models` listing;
- Venice's native `POST /image/generate` (feature `image`) — its own wire,
  not OpenAI's: `width`/`height` in, `{ id, images: [base64], … }` out;
- `POST /audio/speech` (feature `audio`) and `POST /audio/transcriptions`.

Venice's `venice_parameters` block (web search and citations, thinking
control, characters, prompt-cache hints) is a serializable
`VeniceParameters` helper merged through `additional_params` — the same
path every other provider's dialect extras take — rather than a parallel
request abstraction. `venice::CompletionResponse` flattens OpenAI's payload
and keeps Venice's response-only blocks, so `raw_completion` callers still
see the resolved parameter echo (where `web_search_citations` arrive) and
the per-request `cost` that an OpenAI-shaped decode would drop.

Venice's video, image-editing, music, web-augmentation, crypto-RPC,
character, API-key and billing endpoints have no corresponding Rig trait
and are deliberately not wrapped.

Configure with `VENICE_API_KEY` (and optional `VENICE_BASE_URL`).

* test(venice): add cassette coverage recorded against the live API

32 scenarios recorded from real Venice traffic (`RIG_PROVIDER_TEST_MODE=record`),
replayed offline by default: the doubleword-equivalent baseline (completion,
streaming, tools, streaming tools, structured output, extractor, typed prompt
with tools, request hooks, embeddings, and the eleven portable agent-conformance
scenarios) plus Venice-specific coverage — the `venice_parameters` block (web
search on/auto with citations, thinking control, character slug, Venice system
prompt opt-out), embeddings honoring `dimensions`, model listing, image
generation, speech synthesis, transcription, and Venice's flat `{"error": "…"}`
envelope on both the unary and streaming paths.

Harness changes the suite needs:

- register the suite in `PROVIDER_CASSETTE_SUITES`, and require `authorization`
  on recorded Venice requests so the header is provably sent and then scrubbed;
- scrub Venice's `images` array like OpenAI's `b64_json` (same base64 image
  payload; keeping it would commit generated media and inflate the fixture) and
  placeholder the image payload's bare `id`, which no prefix rule recognizes;
- add Venice key spellings to the forbidden-pattern scan;
- a cassette that recorded no request body still matches a *multipart* request:
  the httpmock proxy exports bodies as strings, so a non-UTF-8 upload is
  exported as no body at all. The multipart shape itself is pinned by a unit
  test beside the provider.

Speech synthesis takes the direct-recording path (the one Bedrock's event
streams use) because that same proxy limitation drops binary *responses* — a
recorded speech response replayed as zero bytes.

Recorded, not assumed, and reflected in the tests: Venice answers `/audio/speech`
with RIFF/WAV when no `response_format` is given, though its model metadata
advertises `mp3`; and tool/structured-output scenarios run on a fast
non-reasoning model because Venice's own `function_calling_default`
(`zai-org-glm-4.7`) is a reasoning model whose multi-turn runs hit Venice's
non-streaming gateway timeout.

fix(bedrock): ship invocable model identifiers, and keep provider error bodies the SDK cannot classify (#2309)

* fix(bedrock): ship model identifiers Bedrock can invoke

39 of the crate's 72 model constants could only ever fail. Checked against
`ListFoundationModels` in us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-central-1 and
ap-northeast-1, and invoked with `Converse` in us-east-1:

- 29 identifiers are absent from every region and answer
  `ResourceNotFoundException` ("This model version has reached the end of
  its life") — including every `anthropic.claude-*` constant the crate
  shipped, so Bedrock's flagship model family had no working identifier at
  all, plus the Titan text and image generators, Claude 2/Instant, Llama
  3.2, Jamba Instruct, the older Stability ids and `cohere.command-text`;
- 10 exist but are servable only through a cross-region inference profile,
  so the bare identifier answers `ValidationException` ("Invocation of
  model ID … with on-demand throughput isn't supported"). Two of those
  (`amazon.nova-premier-v1:0`, `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-20250514-v1:0`)
  are retired even through their profile.

Retired identifiers are removed. The profile-only families carry their
`us.` profile identifier, and Anthropic is represented by the current
Claude 4.5/4.6/5 profiles. A `us.` prefix names a region family; callers
outside the US substitute `eu.`/`apac.` (or `global.` where offered),
which the module comment now states.

Every retained identifier was invoked live before being written down.

* fix(bedrock): keep provider error bodies the SDK cannot classify

`SdkError::into_service_error` funnels every failure this SDK version does
not model — an unmodeled exception, a transport that dropped
`x-amzn-errortype`, a dispatch failure — into `Unhandled`, whose `meta()`
is empty and whose message sits on its source. The conversion's catch-all
therefore discarded the service's own words and reported Bedrock's
end-of-life notice as:

    ProviderError("An unexpected error occurred. Verify Internet
                   connection or AWS keys")

with `provider_response_body() == None`.

The raw HTTP body is now the fallback across all four conversions
(converse, converse-stream, invoke-model into image and embedding); a
classified exception's own message still wins, and with neither present
the Rig-authored prose stays a plain `ProviderError` rather than
masquerading as a provider response body.

Found by recording a retired model id live and replaying it: the live run
classified the exception and passed, the replay did not, and the
divergence was this discarded body.

* test(bedrock): record the model-identifier failure modes from the live API

Four scenarios recorded against real Bedrock traffic: a retired identifier
preserving its end-of-life body, a bare profile-only identifier rejected
for on-demand throughput, the same model completing through its
cross-region profile, and the replacement Claude constant completing
end-to-end.

Harness: `x-amzn-errortype` joins the response header allowlist. It is how
the AWS SDKs classify an error response into a modeled exception, so
dropping it made every recorded AWS error replay as an unclassified
`Unhandled` — a cassette could not reproduce the error path it had just
recorded. The value is an exception class name, not account state.

The unclassified path that recording exposed keeps unit coverage, since a
cassette can no longer produce it now that the header survives.

fix(bedrock): raw_completion discards provider-only response data (guardrail trace, request id, service tier) (#2311)

* fix(bedrock): stop raw_completion discarding provider-only response data

`raw_completion` is the escape hatch for everything rig does not
normalize, so its contract is that nothing the provider sent was thrown
away. The conversion from the SDK's `ConverseOutput` matched five fields
and swallowed the rest, losing four:

- `trace` — the guardrail assessment. This is the costly one: a blocked
  turn normalizes to a content-filter finish reason and nothing else, so
  which policy fired, on what text, was unrecoverable;
- `performance_config`;
- `service_tier`;
- the AWS `request_id`, which rides the `x-amzn-RequestId` header and is
  the identifier AWS support asks for.

All four are carried now. The three SDK-typed ones keep the SDK's own
types rather than gaining hand-written mirrors — a guardrail assessment
alone is a dozen types, and a mirror that drifts reintroduces exactly the
silent loss this exists to prevent — and are `#[serde(skip)]` because
those types are not `Serialize`: an in-process caller reads them in full
while a serialized response omits them.

`types::converse_output` and `types::assistant_content` become public.
Both lived behind `pub(crate)` modules, so a caller could not name the
type `raw_completion` returns; an escape hatch whose type is unnameable
is only half an escape hatch.

The SDK's output is `#[non_exhaustive]` with a private field, so the rest
pattern is mandatory and cannot be traded for a compile-time guard. The
field list is pinned by `converse_output_carries_every_sdk_field`.

* feat(bedrock): attach a guardrail configuration to Converse requests

`CompletionModel::with_guardrail(identifier, version, trace)` sets
`guardrailConfig` on every Converse request the model issues, following
the shape of the existing `with_prompt_caching` option.

Requests previously had no way to carry a guardrail at all, which also
made the response-side trace unreachable: Bedrock only returns its
assessment when the request asked for it, so the trace preserved in the
previous commit had no way to be populated for a rig caller.

* test(bedrock): record guardrail trace and request id from the live API

Two scenarios recorded against real Bedrock traffic: a guardrail-blocked
turn whose assessment reaches `raw_completion`, and an ordinary turn
whose AWS request id does. Both were recorded against a guardrail created
for the recording and deleted afterwards.

Harness, both driven by what the recording needed:

- ARNs get their 12-digit account-id segment placeholdered. A guardrail
  assessment echoes the guardrail ARN, which carries the caller's AWS
  account id — a provider account identifier, which cassettes must not
  commit. The rest of the ARN stays readable.
- `x-amzn-requestid` joins the response header allowlist with its value
  placeholdered. The SDK reads the request id off that header and nowhere
  else, so a cassette that dropped it could not replay behavior that
  reads the id — the recording passed live and failed on replay until the
  header survived.

`direct_recorder_omits_sigv4_headers` had pinned the old allowlist
incidentally; its assertion is updated to the new intended behavior while
still proving no SigV4 material is recorded.
