fix(gemini, agent): close the whole output-budget truncation chain, not just the 4096 cap (#2324)

* fix(gemini): stop injecting a hardcoded maxOutputTokens=4096 (#2322)

`GenerationConfig`'s `Default` hardcoded `temperature: Some(1.0)` and
`max_output_tokens: Some(4096)`. Two request paths seeded themselves from
that `Default`, so both silently shipped a 4096-token cap and a pinned
temperature that no caller asked for:

- **native structured output** — the `output_schema` arm of
  `create_request_body`, i.e. every `output_schema` turn;
- **image generation** — the `..Default::default()` request literal.

A caller who set a 16k budget got 4096. Only callers relying on the model
default were affected: an explicit `max_tokens` is applied afterwards and
overwrote the injected value, which is why the plain-agent fix in #2283
did not surface this.

#2283 fixed the same hazard for the `temperature`/`max_tokens` arm and
left a comment spelling out why `Default::default()` must not be used as
a seed — but the `output_schema` arm directly above it kept doing it.
Rather than clear the two fields at a third call site, the footgun is
removed at the root: `Default` is now derived, so it is all-`None`, and
every field is already `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`. A
default config puts nothing on the wire and Gemini applies each model's
own documented limit. The bespoke literal from #2283 collapses back to
`GenerationConfig::default()`.

## Test matrix

Live-recorded against Gemini, asserting on the *request* boundary — the
recorded body is the assertion, and `assert_recorded_sampling_fields`
parses the cassette YAML/JSON rather than substring-matching, so a field
name occurring in a response or a JSON schema cannot skew the result.

| scenario | schema | max_tokens | temperature | recorded generationConfig |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agent_max_tokens_without_additional_params` (C15) | no | 512 | unset | `maxOutputTokens` only |
| `structured_output_without_max_tokens` | yes | unset | unset | neither field |
| `structured_output_with_max_tokens` | yes | 16384 | unset | `maxOutputTokens` only |
| `temperature_without_max_tokens` | no | unset | 0.0 | `temperature` only |
| `nano_banana_image_generation_smoke` | n/a | n/a | n/a | neither field |

The 16384 case pins the reported scenario directly: a budget above the
old hardcoded cap now reaches Gemini intact. C15 and the temperature-only
case cover both halves of the shared seed, so a reintroduced non-`None`
default is caught whichever field it lands on.

## Cassette churn

18 existing Gemini cassettes were re-recorded live. Two changed because
of the bug itself (`structured_output_smoke`,
`nano_banana_image_generation_smoke`); the other 16 changed because their
tests pass `GenerationConfig::default()` through `additional_params`,
which now serializes to `{}` instead of the two injected fields. Request
bodies lose only those fields; response bodies differ because they are
fresh recordings. No test assertions were weakened.

## Not addressed

The streaming path reports a `MAX_TOKENS` turn carrying no content as a
successful, empty completion (`streaming.rs` emits `FinalResponse` where
the non-streaming path raises a `ResponseError`). That is what hid this
bug in production — the truncation surfaced as an unexplained empty
response. `finish_reason: Length` is propagated, so it is detectable but
not enforced. Left for a follow-up since the fix direction is a
maintainer call and is not needed to close #2322.

* fix(agent): preserve the terminal finish reason and reject empty truncated turns (#2322)

Closes the rest of the rig#2322 failure chain. The `Default` fix (previous
commit) stopped Gemini injecting a 4096-token cap; these are the three
defects that made that cap invisible and would hide the next one.

## The reason was lost in rig-agent, not the provider

The Gemini adapter was never at fault: `map_google_finish_reason` maps
`MAX_TOKENS` to `FinishReason::Length` and `StreamFinal::finish_reason`
carries it. The assembler dropped it — the `Final` arm read `usage` and
`saw_text` and discarded the rest, and `finish_reason` appeared nowhere
in `run/`. On the agent API a truncated turn was not merely unenforced,
it was *undetectable*.

`CompletionCall` now carries `finish_reason`, populated on both the
blocking and streamed recorders, sourced from the same terminal record
identity already comes from. Per call rather than per run: a multi-turn
run has N reasons and the truncated one is the diagnostic.

## An empty truncated turn is not an answer

A turn with zero content that reports `Length` or `ContentFilter` now
fails with a `ResponseError` naming the reason, matching what the
blocking Gemini path already did for a content-less candidate. The two
surfaces disagreeing is what let truncation surface as a blank answer.

Deliberately narrow, because the empty-success path is intentional
(`run/mod.rs` documents it, and a test pins it):

- partial output then truncated -> still valid, reason preserved;
- textless with `Stop`/`ToolCalls` -> unchanged;
- `Other` -> not truncation; it is a provider's own wire spelling with
  no normalized meaning, so erroring would fail benign runs.

`final_response_can_remain_empty_for_truly_textless_turns` passes
**untouched**: its mock leaves `finish_reason` unset, so the new rule
cannot fire on it. Verified, not assumed.

## Rig was discarding Gemini's real output limit

`ListModelEntry` parsed `inputTokenLimit` and dropped `outputTokenLimit`,
and the generic `Model` had nowhere to put it — so nothing in the library
knew `gemini-2.5-flash` allows 65536 output tokens, ~16x the hardcoded
4096. `Model::max_output_tokens` fixes that, distinct from
`context_length`. It is **not** sent on requests: omitting an output
limit is what lets the provider apply its own default, and populating it
from the listing would reintroduce a rig-chosen cap by another route.

## Tests

Six scenarios, four synthetic and two live-recorded.

Synthetic (rig-agent), because a provider cannot be made to emit an
exactly-empty `MAX_TOKENS` turn or a safety filter on demand — each says
so in its doc comment per tests/README.md:

- empty + `MAX_TOKENS` -> errors naming the reason
- partial text + `MAX_TOKENS` -> stays valid, reason on the call
- empty + content filter -> errors
- empty + `Other` -> still finalizes

The two guard tests were confirmed to FAIL with the rule disabled, and
the two "stays valid" tests to pass either way — so the pair genuinely
pins the behavior rather than the implementation.

Live-recorded (Gemini):

- thinking-config without `max_tokens` -> `{"thinkingConfig":{...}}`
  alone. This is the pattern that hid #2283 and the one most exposed to
  a restored `Default`, since callers write `..Default::default()`.
- streaming structured output without `max_tokens` -> no sampling fields.

Plus a model-listing assertion against the existing cassette (65536 for
gemini-2.5-flash, >40 models annotated), needing no new recording.

## Verification

4384 workspace tests pass, 0 failures. fmt and clippy
(--all-targets --all-features) clean. **Zero existing cassettes
modified** — the only cassette changes are the two new files.

* fix(agent): a reasoning-only truncated turn is not an answer (#2322)

P1 in this PR's own guard. The rule added in 9e172020 keyed on
`is_empty_assistant_turn`, which is true for only two shapes: no items,
or one empty unannotated text block. A turn carrying **one Reasoning
item and nothing else** is neither, so the guard never fired and the run
finalized successfully with `output == ""`.

That is not a corner case — it is the common shape of rig#2322. Gemini
counts thinking tokens against `maxOutputTokens` (the committed
cassettes show `thoughtsTokenCount` of 176-307 on ordinary prompts), so
a model that exhausts its budget while thinking is cut off *before*
emitting any answer text and the turn carries reasoning, no text. The
headline scenario of the issue — thinking model, small budget, blank
answer — was still broken on the branch that claims to fix it.

Repro against 9e172020: reasoning event + FinalResponse(Length) ->
"FINALIZED SUCCESSFULLY, output=\"\"".

## The fix is a predicate correction, not a wider rule

"Does this turn belong in history" and "did this turn deliver an answer"
are different questions, and they diverge on exactly this shape: a
reasoning-only turn *does* belong in history (the reasoning is real
content worth replaying) but has answered nothing.

`turn_delivered_no_answer` — no tool call, no non-empty text — is the
predicate the guard needed. `is_empty_assistant_turn` is untouched and
still governs the history push, so reasoning is still recorded; the two
now sit beside each other with doc comments stating the distinction.

Tool calls count as delivered: a truncated tool-call turn still routes
to execution rather than erroring.

Behaviour after the swap:

| turn shape        | reason                  | outcome                |
|-------------------|-------------------------|------------------------|
| nothing           | Length / ContentFilter  | error                  |
| reasoning only    | Length / ContentFilter  | error (the fix)        |
| any non-empty text| Length                  | valid, reason kept     |
| reasoning + text  | Length                  | valid, reason kept     |
| tool calls        | Length                  | routes to tools        |
| any               | Stop / ToolCalls / Other| unchanged              |

## Tests

Five synthetic cases, each documenting why it cannot be a cassette (a
provider cannot be made to truncate mid-thought on demand):

- reasoning-only + Length -> errors naming the reason
- reasoning-only + ContentFilter -> errors
- reasoning + text + Length -> valid, reason on the call, text returned
- reasoning-only + Stop -> still finalizes (thought, nothing to add)
- reasoning reaches the consumer before the error, so a truncated
  thinking turn stays debuggable — pins the history-push/guard ordering

Confirmed to fail without the fix: reverting the predicate fails the two
erroring tests while the three others still pass, so the set pins the
behaviour rather than the implementation. This check exists because
9e172020's tests passed against the broken guard — they only ever
scripted zero-content or text-then-truncate, never reasoning-only.

Changelog and MIGRATING wording corrected: both said "produced zero
assistant content", which described the old, wrong predicate.

4389 workspace tests pass (+5), rig-agent lib 502 (+5). fmt and clippy
clean. No cassette churn — this is agent-layer logic and no request
shape changed.

* fix(agent): an image response is an answer (#2322)

P1 reported against 9c1767e2. `turn_delivered_no_answer` classified
image-only turns as "no answer", so a truncated image-generation turn
would error despite having delivered an image.

Repro: `turn_delivered_no_answer(&[AssistantContent::Image(..)])`
returned `true`.

This is not hypothetical. Ten providers emit assistant images, Gemini's
blocking path among them (`PartKind::InlineData` ->
`AssistantContent::image_base64`), and image tokens count against the
same output budget the rest of this PR is about — a truncated image turn
is exactly the combination that hits it.

## Root cause: the catch-all, not the missing arm

The predicate matched `Text` and `ToolCall` and sent everything else to
`_ => false`. That default is backwards. "Not one of the two shapes I
thought of" is not evidence a turn answered nothing, and the wildcard
made the mistake silent: `Image` had existed all along, and any variant
added later would have inherited the same wrong bucket without a word
from the compiler.

The match is now exhaustive with no `_` arm. `Image` is an answer,
`Reasoning` is the single exclusion, and adding an `AssistantContent`
variant breaks this build (verified: E0004 at the predicate) so the
classification has to be made deliberately.

That the same predicate has now been wrong twice — first on `Reasoning`,
then on `Image` — is the argument for the exhaustive match rather than a
third patch.

## Tests

Two unit tests, at the level the defect lives at rather than through a
stream: this is a pure classification decision over a rig-owned enum, no
provider traffic involved, and a variant silently inheriting the wrong
bucket is invisible at the wire level. Both say so in their doc comments.

- every variant's classification, plus mixed shapes (reasoning+image is
  an answer; reasoning+empty-text is not)
- the two turn predicates diverge on exactly one shape (reasoning-only)
  and agree everywhere else — pinning that the divergence is intentional
  and bounded

Confirmed to fail without the fix: restoring `_ => false` fails the
first test on the image assertion.

* fix(agent): correct the divergence doc and drop a dangling error pointer (#2322)

Two P3s reported against b3b8b53f.

## The predicates diverge on two shapes, not one

`turn_delivered_no_answer`'s doc and its test both claimed the only
divergence from `is_empty_assistant_turn` was a reasoning-only turn.
An **empty text block carrying `additional_params`** diverges too:

    is_empty_assistant_turn      = false  (annotated -> recordable)
    turn_delivered_no_answer     = true   (no text -> no answer)

The old test checked three agreeing shapes — `[]`, empty text, real
text — none annotated, so it never touched the case it claimed to
exclude. Same failure as the earlier P1s: the test encoded the
documentation's assumption instead of probing it.

The behaviour was already right; the description was not. Both shapes
are now named in the doc, and the test enumerates the divergent set and
the agreeing set explicitly (now including image and tool-call turns).

## Metadata-only text is not an answer — stated, not implied

The P3 asked for this to be settled explicitly rather than left to fall
out of the predicate's code, so it is now its own test and its own
paragraph of doc.

It is not an answer: `assistant_text_from_choice` concatenates
`text.text` alone, so an annotation-only turn hands the caller `""`. The
metadata (citations, encrypted reasoning references) is worth recording
— and `prompt_request_preserves_metadata_only_text_turn_in_history`
already pins that it is — but it is metadata *about* an answer, never
the answer. A turn truncated in that state delivered nothing.

The test also pins that an annotation does not suppress a real answer
sitting beside it, and notes the run-level consequence if anyone
reclassifies it: whether a truncated annotation-only turn errors or
silently returns "".

## The truncation error pointed at a type that never materialises

The message advised inspecting `PromptResponse::completion_calls`, but
this path returns `Err` — no `PromptResponse` is ever built, so the
advice sent callers somewhere that does not exist. Removed; the reason
is named in the error itself, which is the only place it appears on this
path. A comment records why the pointer must not come back.

`MIGRATING.md`'s reference to `completion_calls` is left alone: it
describes the *success* path (partial output then truncation), where a
`PromptResponse` genuinely is returned.

4392 workspace tests pass. fmt clean, clippy clean under -D warnings.

* fix(agent): reason-appropriate truncation advice, and cover the blocking surface

Addresses the code review of #2324. Three of four findings applied; the
fourth is a design question left for maintainers.

## F1 (medium) — the error gave advice that cannot help

The guard fires for `ContentFilter` as well as `Length`, but the message
ended unconditionally with "the turn was cut short ... raise max_tokens".
For a safety block (Gemini SAFETY/PROHIBITED_CONTENT, Anthropic refusal,
OpenAI content_filter) that is both factually wrong — nothing was cut
short — and actively misleading: it sends the caller to change a setting
that cannot fix a filtered response.

The remedy now branches on the reason. Giving the wrong remedy is worse
than giving none.

Both filter tests only asserted that *some* error occurred, which is why
they did not catch this. They now assert the reason is named and that
`max_tokens` is **not** suggested; the `Length` test asserts it is.

## F3 (low) — the blocking surface had no coverage at all

All nine guard tests drove `stream_prompt`. `MockTurn` had no way to set
a finish reason, so `CompletionResponse::finish_reason()` was always
`None` on the blocking mock and `runner.rs`'s
`.with_finish_reason(resp.finish_reason())` was never exercised —
deleting that line failed nothing.

That is the worst place to have a gap: this PR's premise is that the two
surfaces disagreeing is what let truncation surface as a blank answer.

Adds `MockTurn::with_finish_reason` and three blocking tests (empty +
Length, reasoning-only + Length, partial output keeps the reason on
`completion_calls`). Verified they close the gap: removing the
`runner.rs` line fails all three.

## F4 (low) — an undocumented behaviour narrowing

The guard sits before the `OutputMode::Tool` re-prompt, so an agent with
an output tool that receives an answerless truncated turn now fails
immediately instead of consuming a retry to re-prompt.

Kept as-is and documented rather than reordered: the re-prompt could not
have helped, since the budget or the filter — not the phrasing — is what
stopped the turn, so the retry would truncate again and fail less
specifically. Now stated in both CHANGELOG and MIGRATING.

## F2 (low) — not applied

`Model` is not `#[non_exhaustive]` while `CompletionCall`/`ModelTurn`/
`StreamedTurn` are, so adding a field to it breaks downstream struct
literals. Making it non-exhaustive is a separate, permanent decision
about how callers construct the type — it would forbid struct-literal
construction the type's own doc example teaches — and belongs with the
maintainers rather than inside an output-budget bugfix. Raised on the PR.

fix(gemini): four response-mapping bugs found by live cassette recording (#2328)

* test(gemini): register per-bug cassette matrix wrappers

The three edge matrices that follow each get their own registered
wrapper, so `cassette_files_match_registered_scenarios` pairs one bug's
fixtures with one bug's call sites and a matrix cannot quietly absorb
another's recordings.

Adds the fixture-side assertions those matrices need: read a scenario's
recorded *response* bodies back and state what shape they must (or must
not) carry. A cell whose provider turn stopped producing the shape it is
about would otherwise keep passing while covering nothing.

* fix(gemini): keep the turn when a response carries code-execution parts

Rig lets a caller enable Gemini's built-in code-execution tool by putting
it in `additional_params.tools`; `create_request_body` lifts that array
onto the request. Gemini then answers with `executableCode` and
`codeExecutionResult` parts interleaved with the model's text, and the
blocking mapper had no arm for either kind, so every such turn fell
through to `ResponseError("Response did not contain a message or tool
call")` and the whole response — final text answer included — was
discarded. The streaming adapter skipped the same parts and returned the
answer, so the two transports disagreed about identical bytes.

Those parts now contribute no assistant content rather than failing the
response, which is where OpenAI Responses puts its own hosted-tool items
(`Output::Unknown` maps to no content). Only a part rig cannot account
for at all is still an error, so a genuinely unexpected payload does not
become a silent content drop.

The edge matrix records 22 live cells (blocking and streaming twins
across surfaces, part compositions, models, and sampling knobs) plus 3
unit cells for states a live turn cannot be made to produce. On
origin/main 14 of the 25 fail.

* fix(gemini): stop reporting the chain-of-thought as output text

`thinkingConfig.includeThoughts` makes Gemini return its reasoning in the
*same* `parts` array as the answer, distinguished only by
`"thought": true`. The completion mapper honours that flag; two other
readers of the same payload did not.

`TryFrom<GenerateContentResponse> for TranscriptionResponse` read
`parts.first()`, which with thoughts on is the reasoning — so
`response.text` returned the model's private chain-of-thought and the
transcript sitting in `parts[1]` was dropped. A transcript split across
several text parts lost everything after the first for the same reason.
`ProviderResponseExt::get_text_response` concatenated every text part,
gluing the reasoning onto the answer; rig's other Gemini transport (the
Interactions API) and Anthropic both exclude reasoning there, so the REST
wire was the odd one out.

Both now read through `visible_text_parts`, the one home for the skip
rule, and the transcript is every visible text part rather than only the
first — joined without an invented separator, because Gemini's split
points are not sentence boundaries.

The edge matrix records 18 live cells across both readers, four model
families, and both thinking dialects, plus 6 unit cells. On origin/main
17 of the 24 fail.

* fix(gemini): defer the streaming terminal record to EOF

`GeminiRestAdapter::interpret` treated any chunk carrying a
`finishReason` as the provider completing the turn and pushed the
terminal record there; the shared driver stops reading as soon as it sees
one. Gemini's `streamGenerateContent` does not honour that assumption:
when a built-in tool runs a round it emits an *intermediate*
`finishReason` and keeps streaming. A recorded two-round code-execution
turn reads

  [executableCode] [codeExecutionResult] [executableCode + finishReason]
  [codeExecutionResult] [text] [text + finishReason]

so rig ended the stream on the third frame, dropped the model's entire
answer, and still yielded a terminal record reporting a clean `STOP` —
while the blocking twin of the same request returned the whole answer.

The terminal is now held until EOF. That is deferral, not synthesis: the
`WireAdapter::finish` contract names "a terminal the provider *did*
signal earlier … whose usage trailer arrives later" as exactly this case.
EOF with no `finishReason` at all is still truncation and still yields no
terminal record, a transport error still drops partials, and an in-band
tool-protocol failure still short-circuits the stream without acquiring
one. Holding the record also means the terminal carries the last reason,
usage, and metadata the stream reported rather than the first.

The edge matrix records 12 live cells — including a cross-family control
showing gemini-3-flash does *not* emit the intermediate finish — and 12
unit cells for shapes the provider cannot be asked for. On origin/main 13
of the 24 fail.

* test(gemini): state the truncation trade-off in the terminal-deferral matrix

* fix(gemini): keep an empty transcription text part convertible

Scanning every visible part instead of only the first made "no text" a

whose text part is genuinely empty converted before this branch and must
keep converting: the structural question is whether the candidate has any
visible text part at all. Pinned by a unit cell, since Gemini answers the

the shape `streaming.rs` already documents and handles — and the blocking
mapper attached the signature only on the `thought: true` arm, so the
`else` branch dropped it. This branch's own `blocking_code_execution_on_
gemini_3_flash` fixture carries exactly that: a text part with a
signature and no flag. The signature is replay-required state Gemini
validates (`MISSING_THOUGHT_SIGNATURE`), and only `Reasoning` round-trips
it back onto a request.

Blocking now produces the signature-only reasoning block the streaming
adapter has always produced for these bytes — measured against the
streamed twin of the same fixture, not assumed.

Addresses the rest of the review too: the deferred terminal's

and the redundant `#[cfg(test)]` on the unit modules is gone.

`generateContent` answers `{"content":{"role":"model"}}` — content

any part is produced (confirmed live with `maxOutputTokens: 1`). The

The re-review caught that the first attempt at this claimed parity it did

fix(anthropic): two stop_sequence bugs found by live cassette recording (#2329)

* fix(anthropic): carry `stop_sequence` on the streamed terminal record

Anthropic's terminal `message_delta` reports which of the caller's
`stop_sequences` actually matched:

    {"delta":{"stop_reason":"stop_sequence","stop_sequence":"charlie"},...}

`MessageDelta` parsed that field and the adapter then dropped it —
`StreamingCompletionResponse` had no slot for it. So `raw_stream`
answered a request with strictly less than `raw_completion` answered the
same request with: the blocking `CompletionResponse::stop_sequence` has
carried the value all along. Anthropic strips the matched sequence from
the text, so the wire frame is its only source; a streamed caller could
learn that *a* sequence fired and never which one.

Add the field and stamp it from the frame that carries it.

Recorded with a 26-cell live matrix under
`tests/cassettes/anthropic/stop_sequence_terminal_matrix/` plus two
serde unit cells: which of several sequences fired, sequences containing
newlines / spaces / punctuation / non-ASCII, case sensitivity, the
empty-content match, coexistence with tools, prompt caching, a system
prompt and a second model, blocking twins, the adjacent normalized and
agent stream paths, and controls proving every other terminal kind still
reports no sequence. Each cell re-derives its premise from its own
fixture bytes.

* fix(anthropic): accept a completed turn that stopped on a sequence before emitting anything

Anthropic strips the sequence it stopped on. When the match is the first
thing the model produces, the turn comes back 200 with:

    {"content":[],"stop_reason":"stop_sequence","stop_sequence":"alpha",...}

`CompletionResponse::normalize` carved out exactly one legal empty case —
`end_turn` — and routed every other empty response through
`require_non_empty_response`. A completed provider turn therefore became
`ResponseError("Response contained no message or tool call (empty)")`,
taking the usage, message id, transport request id and finish reason down
with it. The streamed twin of the same request already finished cleanly
with an empty choice, so this was also a blocking/streaming divergence
with the blocking side broken.

Extend the carve-out to `stop_sequence` and leave every other empty
response guarded.

The carve-out is deliberately not widened past its evidence: a live probe
showed `max_tokens` truncation always emits at least one token, and
`tool_use` / `pause_turn` / `refusal` / no-stop-reason empties stay
rejected — pinned by unit cells because no provider turn produces them on
demand.

Recorded with an 18-cell live matrix under
`tests/cassettes/anthropic/empty_stop_sequence_matrix/` plus seven unit
cells: every caller surface (`raw_completion` + `normalize`, `completion`,
agent `prompt`, the streamed and agent-streamed twins), sequence shapes
that can match at position zero, coexistence with a system prompt, tools
and prompt caching, a second model, identity and usage survival, and a
control proving content that *was* produced is never swallowed.

* fix(anthropic): keep the empty-turn carve-out inside its evidence, and tighten the matrices

Independent review of the branch found no correctness defect in either fix but
did find that the second one was wider than the commit message claimed, plus
several test-hygiene issues. Addressed here.

**The carve-out was wider than its evidence (the substantive one).** Keying it
on `stop_reason` alone accepted `{"content":[],"stop_reason":"stop_sequence",
"stop_sequence":null}` as a completed empty turn. Every recorded stop-sequence
terminal names the sequence that fired — 38 across the corpus, none null — so a
turn claiming the reason while naming nothing is the malformed shape the guard
exists for. The `stop_sequence` arm now additionally requires
`stop_sequence.is_some()`; `end_turn` is untouched. This matters most for the
Anthropic-compatible gateways sharing this mapping (minimax, moonshot,
xiaomimimo, zai), which are the likeliest to report a stop reason without its
companion field. Pinned by a new matrix unit cell and by the in-crate loop; both
fail if the tightening is reverted.

**`empty_non_end_turn_response_still_errors` no longer described the rule.**
Replaced with `empty_response_outside_the_legal_terminals_still_errors`, which
loops over `tool_use` / `max_tokens` / `refusal` / `pause_turn` / no-reason /
sequence-less `stop_sequence`, plus a positive case for the legal one.

**A matrix assertion was vacuous.** The prompt-caching cell asserted
`usage.cache_creation.is_some()`, but Anthropic reports that bucket on every
`message_start` — the non-caching cells record the same all-zero buckets, so it
passed with `with_prompt_caching()` removed. Replaced with a read of the
recorded *request* for its `cache_control` marker, which is what actually
distinguishes the cell.

**Two wrappers were byte-identical copies of `with_anthropic_cassette`.** They
now delegate to it, so they cannot drift when it gains policy. Their doc comments
no longer claim the fixture path depends on them — it comes from the scenario
string; what the separate names buy is a per-bug cassette-safety registry entry.

Also: `identity_survives_empty_stop` derives the responding model from its own
fixture instead of hardcoding a dated snapshot id, and `recorded_response_body`
now refuses a base64-encoded body rather than silently misreading one.

* docs(changelog): record the two anthropic stop_sequence fixes (#2329)

* test(anthropic): restore the model pass-through pin and tighten the matrices further

Second review round of the fix-up diff found no P1 and confirmed the carve-out
tightening is correct and genuinely pinned. It did find that the previous

fix(mistral): four provider bugs found by live cassette recording (#2331)

* fix(mistral): send non-text content instead of dropping it

MistralExt::finalize_request_body flattened every message content array
with the text-only helper, which keeps only parts carrying a
text/refusal key. Images, audio and documents were therefore removed
from the request before it was sent, and the caller got an ordinary
completion answering a prompt its content never reached (#2290).

Content is now rendered as Mistral's own chunks: image_url forwards
unchanged, input_audio collapses to the bare-string payload its schema
documents, and OpenAI's file part maps onto document_url for inline
base64 -- carrying the filename in document_name -- or onto Mistral's
file chunk, which names an uploaded file_id at the top level rather than
nesting it. That makes vision and document Q&A reachable through rig on
Mistral for the first time (#2291).

Textuality is decided on the type tag rather than the presence of a text
key, so a part naming a chunk kind is converted as that kind even if it
also carries text; deciding on the key alone would flatten the chunk
away, which is the drop this path exists to prevent.

Text-only content still flattens to Mistral's plain string, so every
existing fixture's request shape is unchanged. Content Mistral has no
chunk for -- video, and any part type a future conversion adds -- now
fails with a ConversionError instead of being silently removed.

* test(mistral): record the multimodal content matrix for #2290

26 recorded cells behind a dedicated wrapper, covering images, audio and
documents across blocking/streaming, raw model/agent, two model
families, replayed history, a configured tool, and the text-only
controls that pin the plain-string shape the fix must not move. Nine
unit cells cover the fail-closed and exact-wire-shape paths, where the
point is that no request is built and so there is no traffic to record.

Each cell asserts its premise against its own recorded *request* bytes:
this bug lives on the outbound side, so a cell that stopped putting its
chunk on the wire fails rather than passing while covering nothing.

Co-authored-by: css521 <42376488+css521@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(mistral): repair verify() and capture the transport request id

Two defects found by probing the live API against the provider config.

VERIFY_PATH was `/models`, but Mistral's client base URL is the bare
host, so every path carries its own `/v1` -- `completion_path` and
MistralModelLister already do. `GET /models` is a gateway 404 ("no Route
matched with those values"), so `Client::verify()` failed for every key,
valid or not.

REQUEST_ID_HEADER was left at its conservative None default although
Mistral reports a transport request id on every response, labelled
`mistral-correlation-id` (and mirrored as `x-kong-request-id`), so
`provider_request_id` was always None on completions, streams and
errors alike.

The existing response-identity cell asserted the second one as the
intended contract ("Mistral sends no request-id header"). It could not
have caught the gap: the header was not on the cassette harness's
response-header allowlist, so the recorded fixture had no id in it to
find and the assertion held against evidence the recording had removed.

* test(mistral): record the verify and request-id cells

Three recorded cells, all failing on origin/main: verify() against the
versioned models route, and the transport request id on the blocking
response and the streaming terminal.

The harness's response-header allowlist gains `mistral-correlation-id`
so a fixture can carry the evidence these cells read; without it the
header is scrubbed away and the cells can only ever observe None.

* fix(providers): treat model_length as truncation, not a natural stop

Mistral spells context-window exhaustion `model_length`. The shared
OpenAI-compatible finish-reason mapper had no arm for it, so it fell
through to FinishReason::Other("model_length") and a turn cut off by the
context window was indistinguishable from one that simply had nothing
more to say. rig-agent's truncating_finish_reason deliberately excludes
Other, so its truncation handling never fired for it either.

Confirmed live against voxtral-small-latest (32768-token context):
a 32,424-token prompt with max_tokens 4096 returned finish_reason
"model_length" with total_tokens 32768 and completion_tokens 344 --
generation stopped dead on the ceiling with most of the output budget
unspent.

OpenRouter's own mapper already folds the same spelling into Length; the
spelling is Mistral-originated and unused by the other providers on the
shared mapper, so one vocabulary is kept rather than two.

* fix(mistral): rebuild the image chunk instead of forwarding it

Review follow-ups on the content normalization.

The image branch was the only one that forwarded its part whole. Every
Mistral chunk forbids unknown fields, so a stray sibling key riding on an
image part would have 422'd the entire request -- and the unit test added
for exactly that input class asserted the stray key was *preserved*,
pinning a body Mistral rejects as correct. The chunk is now rebuilt from
the fields Mistral names, like every other branch, and the test asserts
that shape.

Also: finalize_request_body is now idempotent over the chunks it emits
(a public trait method should not report content rig itself built as
unsupported); the audio error no longer mentions a URL form nothing
accepts; the file-mapping test no longer claims live coverage for the
file_id half, which is pinned by shape only; and the "fails closed"
docs name the all-text flattening exception rather than reading as
unconditional.

On the test side, two cells whose recorded requests were byte-identical
to a sibling's (~46 KB of duplicated base64) are folded into that
sibling, and the module doc now states what the assert_recorded_*
helpers actually police -- the harness's request matching is what fails a
regressed cell in replay; the helpers guard the recording.

* test(mistral): cover the request-id contract on 4xx as well

The contract has to hold on failures too -- an error that eats the id is
as unrecoverable as one that eats the body -- and Mistral does send
mistral-correlation-id on 4xx. Two cells: a 400 from an unroutable model
(Mistral's {"object":"error",...} envelope, asserted alongside the

The bogus-key wrapper inlines ProviderCassette::start rather than

fix(openai): six wire-level defects found by live cassette recording (#2332)

* fix(openai): surface Chat Completions refusals, and cap reasoning models

Two defects in the same two files, both found by recording live traffic and
reading the bytes back.

**Refusals are dropped.** OpenAI spells a structured-output refusal as a
sibling of `content` (`{"content": null, "refusal": "…"}`) and streams it on
`delta.refusal`; rig modeled only the `refusal` content *part*, which is the
Responses API's shape and which chat completions never sends. So a refused
turn failed with the opaque `Response did not contain a valid message or tool
call` when blocking, streamed no text at all, and could not be converted back
into rig history — while `get_text_response` already fell back to the field,
and the same request through the Responses surface worked. All four paths now
share one rule, `assistant_refusal_fallback`, which takes its emptiness
verdict from the wire parts so no two callers can disagree.

**Reasoning models cannot be capped.** Every `gpt-5`-and-up and `o`-series
model rejects the legacy `max_tokens` outright ("Unsupported parameter … Use
'max_completion_tokens' instead"), so `agent.max_tokens(n)` could not succeed
against them at all. The modern spelling is scoped to those families through
the new `OpenAICompatibleProvider::requires_modern_output_cap`, not applied to
the endpoint: this same extension is how rig reaches OpenAI-compatible servers
(mistral.rs, vLLM, llama.cpp, gateways), and OpenAI's own older models still
take the legacy field. Nothing outside the reasoning families changes a byte —
no pre-existing fixture in the tree moved.

Both fixes are covered by their own recorded edge matrix (18 and 22 cells) plus
unit cells for the wire shapes live traffic will not produce on demand.

* fix(providers): let a truncated OpenAI-compatible turn reach the caller

A reasoning model whose output-token cap is consumed entirely by hidden
reasoning answers with an empty message and `finish_reason: "length"`. The
shared chat-completions normalizer rejected that wholesale — `Response
contained no message or tool call (empty)` — discarding both the reason and
the usage, so a caller could not tell "you hit the cap" from "the provider
misbehaved", and rig-agent's purpose-built message for exactly this state was
unreachable behind the provider-layer failure.

Three sibling paths already got it right: the Responses API deliberately lets
a contentless `status: incomplete` turn through, the chat-completions
streaming path yields a terminal record with the reason regardless of what the
stream produced, and the same model through the Responses surface therefore
disagreed with the Chat Completions surface for one rig-level request.

The unary path now applies the same rule, named once on
`FinishReason::truncated_output`: a turn the provider *cut short* (`length`,
`content_filter`) may be contentless and carries its reason to the caller; a
turn that *ran to completion* with nothing in it is still a provider defect.
rig-agent had an open-coded copy of that predicate for deciding whether an
answerless turn has a remedy worth naming — the same question, so it now reads
the shared one and the two cannot drift.

Covered by a 16-cell recorded matrix across both API surfaces, both
transports, three reasoning families and the agent level, plus unit cells
enumerating the accept/reject rule over the whole finish-reason vocabulary.

* fix(openai): repair the image-generation request body

Two defects in one twelve-line body builder.

Rig added `"response_format": "b64_json"` for every model outside a hardcoded
`gpt-image-1`/`1.5`/`2` allowlist, but the endpoint now rejects that field for
*all* models (`400 Unknown parameter: 'response_format'`). Every other image
model OpenAI serves — `gpt-image-1-mini`, `chatgpt-image-latest`, and any dated
snapshot of an allowlisted model such as `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21` — therefore
could not generate an image at all. The field is also unnecessary: the endpoint
returns `data[].b64_json` by default, which is what rig already decodes.

`ImageGenerationRequest::additional_params` was never merged into the body, so
`quality`, `background`, `output_format`, `user` and the rest were silently
inert for OpenAI while xAI's and Gemini's image bodies honored the same field.
Merging it last also restores the escape hatch the first fix removes: an
OpenAI-compatible images endpoint that still wants `response_format` can be
handed it explicitly.

Covered by a 16-cell recorded matrix. The rejected cells are deliberate: an
error naming the caller's own parameter is direct evidence the parameter
reached OpenAI, and recording one costs nothing.

* docs(changelog): record the four openai fixes

* fix(openai): keep the transcription endpoint's usage

`/v1/audio/transcriptions` reports what a transcription cost beside the
transcript, in one of two shapes depending on how the model bills: `whisper-1`
by audio duration (`{"type":"duration","seconds":6}`), the `gpt-4o-transcribe`
family by token (`{"type":"tokens","input_tokens":54,…}`). Rig's response type
modeled only `{ text }`, and the normalized `TranscriptionResponse` has no
usage slot either — so the accounting was dropped even from the raw provider
response, which is the surface that exists to carry provider-specific fields.
A caller had no way to learn what a transcription cost.

The usage is matched by its distinguishing fields rather than by the `type`
tag, with a verbatim catch-all last, so a third shape — or a compatible
provider's own — is carried through instead of failing the whole
transcription. The response type is shared with Groq and Azure OpenAI, which
gain the same field.

Covered by an 8-cell matrix that enumerates the space rather than sampling it:
both billing shapes × both client extensions, plus the request shaping that
decides which shape comes back and the two absence cases. The shapes no live
model produces are unit cells beside the fix.

* fix(openai): correct claims and one output shape found by cold review

An independent review of the branch found one invariant the code did not hold
and several claims that were imprecise. All verified against the code before
changing anything.

**The refusal fix is not "one rule" across four paths.** The three unary paths
share `assistant_refusal_fallback`, a *whole-message* rule. The streaming path
cannot: it decides per delta, before it knows whether text arrives later, so it
applies the same intent per delta. On the one shape where they would differ —
a turn mixing text and a refusal, which this wire has never been observed to
send, because a refusal turn holds `content` at `null` for its whole length —
blocking reports only the text and streaming both in arrival order. That is now
stated in both doc comments and pinned by the per-delta unit cell, rather than
claimed away.

**History conversion could disagree with normalization.** `TryFrom<Message>`
pushed the refusal and then appended the wire parts unfiltered, so
`{"content": "", "refusal": "R"}` produced `[text("R"), text("")]` where
`normalize` produced `[text("R")]` — and the stray empty block went back on the
wire on replay. The fallback and the parts are now either/or, which they always
were in meaning: the fallback fires only when no part carried text.

**The quoted error string was wrong.** A refused turn failed with
`Response contained no message or tool call (empty)`, not `Response did not
contain a valid message or tool call`. The string is what a user searches for,
so both the changelog and the matrix doc now quote the one the code produces.

Also: the image-generation doc claimed a property of "the endpoint" ("returns
b64_json by default") that is really a property of the models it currently
serves — the verified claim is narrower and stronger, that `response_format`
is not in the endpoint's request schema at all, which it rejects before it even
looks at the model. Azure's image body drops `additional_params` the same way
OpenAI's did, and Azure fronts the same reasoning models without the output-cap
fix; both are now named as known gaps rather than implied to be covered, with
the reason Azure cannot share the predicate (its model handle is a deployment
name, which carries no family to classify). `chat_streaming_and_blocking_agree_
on_refusal` is renamed to what it actually asserts. New public API is listed
under `### Added`, and `MIGRATING.md` documents the empty-choice change for
callers who index `CompletionResponse::choice` directly.

* fix(openai): close the findings from the focused re-review

A second review, covering the transcription fix and the previous round's
fix-up, found seven things. All verified before changing anything.

**The claim I thought I had fixed was still in one file.** The refusal
matrix's own module doc still said the fix "routes the four paths through one
rule" — the previous commit had edited the sentence around it and left the
claim itself standing, in exactly the file a reader goes to for the matrix's
account of the fix. It now says what the code does, as the changelog and both
source doc comments already did.

**The either/or fix had no regression guard.** `{"content": "", "refusal":
"R"}` is the only input that distinguishes the old behavior from the new, and
every refusal unit cell used `"content": null`, which produces an empty parts
vector and cannot tell them apart. Two cells now pin both sides of the branch.

**The images claim outran its evidence.** The doc asserted that
`response_format` is rejected *before* the endpoint looks at the model, and no
fixture paired a nonexistent model with the field — the one experiment that
shows it. Cell 17 records it: the error names the field and never mentions the
model. That ordering is why the old allowlist was fatal, so it is worth having.

**Azure is worse than disclosed.** Its image body hardcodes `response_format`
*and* drops `additional_params`, so an Azure caller cannot even work around the
former. The doc named only the smaller gap. Fixing it blind is the kind of
guess this change set is trying not to ship, so it is now named accurately
instead.

**The transcription usage enum selected on the wrong thing.** Untagged struct
variants ignore unknown fields, so `Duration` matched any payload carrying a
numeric `seconds` — a future `{"type":"tokens","seconds":6,…}` would have
decoded as a duration and silently dropped every token count, with the
catch-all never firing. Each variant now pins the wire's own `type`.

**`input_token_details` was sitting unmodeled in the branch's own fixtures** —
the very defect the transcription fix is about. It is now kept, and it matters:
audio and text input tokens bill at different rates, so `input_tokens` alone
does not tell a caller what a turn cost.

**The transcription matrix claimed a dimension it cannot observe.** The harness
cannot match a multipart request body, so no cell there can pin request
shaping; that belongs to the shared multipart builder's unit tests, which the
module doc now points at. Two cells are renamed to what they assert, one of
them now checking the usage *variant* rather than its mere presence — it is the
cell whose fixture also carries a top-level `duration`, so it is where a
variant-selection regression would surface first.

* docs(changelog): point the openai entries at the opened PR

* fix(providers): honor additional_params in the shared text-to-speech body

The same defect as the image body's, one endpoint over, found by the sweep
that followed. The *default*
`RawAudioGenerationProvider::audio_generation_request_body` never merged
`AudioGenerationRequest::additional_params`, so the field was silently inert
for whoever inherited that default — OpenAI included.

What makes it a defect rather than a design: every provider that overrides the
body already merges the field (xAI, OpenRouter, Venice). Three siblings do the
right thing and the default does not.

The parameters are not cosmetic. Measured against the live endpoint,
`response_format: "wav"` returns a 21 KB RIFF payload where the default returns
an 8 KB MP3, and `instructions` steers delivery on the `gpt-4o-mini-tts`
family. The matrix asserts the returned *container* by magic bytes, which is
the only thing that shows a parameter took effect rather than merely appearing
in a request body.

These scenarios need the direct recorder — the endpoint answers with raw audio,
and the httpmock proxy exports bodies as strings, so a recorded speech response
would replay as zero bytes. That client already existed for Venice's TTS
scenario; rather than copy ninety lines of it, this moves it into the cassette
module and points both suites at one definition. It goes there rather than into
the shared test-support module on purpose: eleven provider targets include that
module without the cassette one, and an import of `crate::cassettes` from there
does not resolve for them.

Two cells were designed and dropped with their reasons in the file: an invalid
`response_format` cannot be recorded at all, because the direct-recording path
captures no interaction for a non-success response; and `tts-1` accepts and
silently ignores `instructions`, so the rejection that cell would have asserted
does not happen.

Azure OpenAI overrides this body and drops the field too. Left alone for the
same reason as its other two gaps: a fix that cannot be recorded against Azure
would be a guess.

refactor: remove #[non_exhaustive] from the workspace (#2335)

* refactor: remove #[non_exhaustive] from the workspace

Strips all 53 `#[non_exhaustive]` attributes across rig-core, rig-agent,
rig-bedrock and rig-candle. Public structs read as plain data again:
struct literals, functional update and exhaustive matches all work from
any crate.

This is permissive, so it is not a breaking change — `cargo semver-checks`
against the previous commit reports 196/196 pass, "no semver update
required". The trade it makes is the reverse of the old one: from here, a
new field on any of these structs or a new variant on any of these enums
is a breaking change, and the attribute cannot be reintroduced outside a
breaking window.

Fallout, all in the same commit so every commit compiles under CI's
`-D warnings`:

- Two matches over `ReasoningContent` covered all four variants behind a
  wildcard that is now unreachable (`tests/common/reasoning.rs`, shared by
  26 test binaries, and `tests/core/streaming_conformance.rs`). Both
  wildcards were already dead at runtime; they are deleted.
- Three rustdoc comments asserted the attribute as the reason to use a
  constructor (`ProviderResponseError`, `ProviderCapabilities`,
  `ModelSelection::new`). Rewritten to recommend the constructors on their
  merits, which is still true and still the better form.
- `gpt_5_6_reasoning.rs` round-tripped a `Reasoning` through serde purely
  because the type was non-exhaustive; it is a struct literal now, which
  is the readability this change is for.

Comments referring to the AWS SDK's own `#[non_exhaustive]` types
(rig-bedrock `converse_output.rs`, `providers/internal/wire.rs`) are
untouched — those attributes belong to aws-sdk-bedrockruntime.

* docs: record the non_exhaustive removal

CHANGELOG entry (not marked breaking — it is permissive) plus a MIGRATING
section covering the one thing downstream code may have to change (delete
now-unreachable wildcard arms), the wasm/native caveat on `CandleError`,
the invariant this widens on `StreamFinal` / `CompletionResponse`, and the
list of shipped guidance the removal supersedes.

fix: three model-listing and usage bugs found by live cassette recording (anthropic, gemini) (#2334)

* fix(anthropic)!: carry extended-thinking tokens into normalized usage

Anthropic reports the tokens Claude spent thinking as
`usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`, and neither `Usage` nor the
streaming `PartialUsage` modeled the field — so serde dropped it and
`anthropic_usage_totals` left `completion::Usage::reasoning_tokens` at 0 on
every turn, blocking and streaming alike.

`reasoning_tokens` is not a field this provider had no home for: its rustdoc
names "Anthropic extended thinking" as one of the things it counts, and both
Gemini (`thoughts_token_count`) and DeepSeek
(`completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`) populate it. An Anthropic
thinking turn reported 0 while the response said 1167 — a caller comparing
reasoning spend across providers saw Anthropic as free.

The value is a *breakdown* of `output_tokens`, not a sibling of it, so it
populates `reasoning_tokens` without entering `total_tokens`; adding it would
double-count. This matches how Gemini and DeepSeek treat theirs. The
parameter is required on the shared `anthropic_usage_totals` rather than
defaulted, so the streaming path cannot silently skip it.

Thirteen already-recorded fixtures carry the field, ten with a non-zero value
(7 to 1167 tokens), across blocking, streaming, adaptive, redacted, and
multi-block thinking — so the regression evidence is real recorded traffic
rather than hand-built usage structs.

BREAKING: `anthropic::completion::Usage` gains `output_tokens_details` and
`anthropic::streaming::PartialUsage` gains the same field. Neither is
`#[non_exhaustive]`, so code constructing them with a full struct literal
must add the field.

* fix(anthropic): stop the model-listing pagination loop from spinning forever

`list_all` ended its cursor loop on `has_more`, then assigned the page's
`last_id` — an `Option` — to the cursor. A page reporting `has_more: true`
with no `last_id` therefore set the cursor back to `None` and re-requested
the *uncursored first page*, which answered the same way: an unbounded loop
re-fetching page 1 and appending its models on every pass, growing memory
until the process died. Not a truncated list — a hang.

Gemini's lister, the only other paginating one in the repo, already breaks on
the cursor's absence rather than on a flag. Anthropic now does the same and
warns, since without a cursor there is no next page to ask for. Anthropic
pairs the two fields, but the Anthropic-compatible gateways sharing this
client are exactly the sources that report a flag without its companion
field.

The happy path had no coverage at all — the one recorded `models` cassette
answers `has_more: false`, so the loop body never ran — so this also adds the
multi-page cursor test that pins `after_id` onto each follow-up request.

* test(anthropic): exhaustive matrix for extended-thinking usage

27 recorded cells plus 4 unit cells, covering the cross-product of transport
(blocking × streaming), thinking mode (fixed budget, adaptive, off), payload
shape (tools advertised, tool_use terminal, system preamble, prompt caching,
redacted thinking, max_tokens truncation), budget size, model family, and the
adjacent normalized-stream and agent surfaces.

Each recorded cell asserts the parsed `reasoning_tokens` equals **its own
fixture's** recorded `thinking_tokens`, read back after the wrapper returns
(record mode writes the fixture on the way out, so an in-body read would
assert against the previous recording). A cell whose turn stops thinking
therefore fails rather than passing vacuously.

Recording surfaced two live-API constraints, both now pinned rather than
worked around:

- Opus 4.8 rejects `thinking.type.enabled` outright, taking `adaptive` plus
  `output_config.effort` instead, so the second model family is covered on
  the adaptive path.
- Adaptive thinking may decline to think at all. Opus 4.7 answers even the
  multi-step prompt without thinking and reports the bucket *present and
  zero* — a different wire shape from thinking-off, which omits the bucket
  entirely. Both reach `reasoning_tokens == 0` through different serde paths
  (`Some(0)` vs `None`), so each gets its own cell and its own assertion
  rather than one lenient "absent or zero" check.

* fix(anthropic): treat an empty listing cursor as absent, and enumerate the loop

An empty `last_id` is as unusable as a missing one and would loop the same
way; rig reads every other provider-reported identifier with the same
empty-means-absent rule. Completes the termination matrix to all seven
reachable combinations, documented in the suite's doc comment along with why
none of them can be a live recording.

* test(anthropic): cover streamed server-tool blocks against real traffic

The inventory's largest coverage gap: streaming.rs models `server_tool_use`,
`web_search_tool_result` and `code_execution_tool_result` on
`content_block_start`/`content_block_stop`, and assembles a server tool's
`input_json_delta` fragments — but every recorded `content_block_start` in
the suite was `text`, `tool_use`, `thinking` or `redacted_thinking`, so that
assembly had only hand-built unit streams behind it.

Records one live streaming web-search turn and its blocking twin. **No bug
found** — rig surfaces both block kinds on both paths — so this is coverage,
not a fix. Recording it was the only way to know.

Each cell reads its own fixture's `content_block_start` frames back and fails
if the provider stops producing server-tool blocks, so it cannot decay into
asserting an ordinary text turn.

* test(anthropic): satisfy clippy in the reasoning-usage matrix helpers

* docs(changelog): record the two anthropic fixes (#2334)

* test(anthropic): cover PDF page-location citations against real traffic

`Citation`'s hand-written serde has five locator variants and only two —
`char_location` and `web_search_result_location` — had ever been recorded.
`page_location` is the shape a PDF produces, and the recorded PDF scenarios
never enabled citations, so that variant had unit coverage only.

Records a citations-enabled URL PDF turn. **No bug found** — the variant
decodes correctly, with 1-indexed, non-inverted page ranges and quoted text —
so this is coverage, not a fix. The cell reads its own fixture back and fails
if the response stops carrying `page_location`, so it cannot decay into
asserting some other locator shape.

* test(anthropic): fix two vacuous matrix cells and scrub a leaked citation index

Cold review of the branch found three real problems, all in the test layer.

**The `max_tokens` truncation cells never truncated.** Both fixtures answered
`stop_reason: end_turn` — the request allowed 1030 tokens against a 1024
thinking budget and the turn finished in ~220 — so the pair covered exactly
the same shape as the plain budget cells while being named for a dimension
they did not exercise. Precisely the vacuous cell the module doc promises
cannot exist. They now use a prompt whose answer overruns the ceiling (which
must sit above `budget_tokens`, so the answer has to be the long part, not
the thinking), and each reads `stop_reason` back from its own fixture and
asserts `max_tokens`.

**The agent cell never touched the agent.** It built a raw
`model.completion_request(...)` identical to `blocking_with_preamble`, down to
byte-identical fixtures. It now drives `client.agent(...).prompt(...)
.extended_details()` and reads `completion_calls[].usage`, which is separate
plumbing from a `CompletionResponse`'s own usage.

**A committed fixture leaked a stable plaintext identifier.** Anthropic's
web-search citation `encrypted_index` base64-decodes to a protobuf containing
a UUID that is identical across separate calls, and it was committed verbatim
while its sibling `encrypted_content` was already scrubbed. Added
`encrypted_index` to `SENSITIVE_STRING_KEYS` and re-recorded the three
affected fixtures — including one pre-existing `opus_4_8` scenario, which is
churn the scrub-policy change requires.

Also corrects three doc comments that claimed more than the code does: the
pagination guard's justification (the four Anthropic-compatible gateways do
not share this lister — a caller pointing the Anthropic client at a gateway
base URL is the real reachable path), a copy-pasted test comment describing
the wrong row, and the claim that unit cell 31 pins the no-carry-forward
decision (the streamed cells do). `recorded_streamed_thinking_tokens` now
asserts a single terminal frame instead of silently taking the first.

Left unfixed and reported instead: `srvtoolu_` ids are not scrubbed, unlike
`toolu_`. Adding the prefix would rewrite a *matched request* body in a
pre-existing scenario, so it needs its own change.

* fix(gemini): stop the model-listing pagination loop on an empty cursor

Surfaced by reviewing the Anthropic fix against its sibling: Gemini's lister
terminates on the cursor's absence, which is the right rule, but reads the
cursor verbatim — so `nextPageToken: ""` is `Some("")`, not `None`. The loop
then re-sends an empty `pageToken`, gets the same page back, and never
returns. Same unbounded-loop class as the Anthropic bug, reached by a
different route.

`parse_models_page` now reads an empty cursor as absent, matching how every
other provider-reported identifier in rig is read. Without the guard the new
test reports `left: Some(""), right: None`.

Also percent-encodes Anthropic's `after_id` instead of interpolating it into
the query string, as Gemini's lister already does for `pageToken`. Anthropic's
model ids are URL-safe today, so this is about not depending on that.

* docs(changelog): record the gemini listing fix (#2334)

* fix: finish the fixture scrub and close the non-advancing cursor case

Re-review of the previous fix-up found the scrub had not actually finished
and the changelog claim was broader than the code.

**The leaked identifier was still in the tree.** The same stable UUID lives in
`encrypted_stdout` — the code-execution sibling of the `encrypted_index` key
just scrubbed — in a pre-existing `opus_4_8` fixture. The earlier "it's gone"
check could not see it: the UUID is only ever base64-encoded in fixtures, so
grepping the plaintext matches nothing even in the files that leak it. The
right query is the encoded fragment. Both keys are now on
`SENSITIVE_STRING_KEYS` with their squashed twins (the list matches on a
lowercased-but-not-underscore-stripped key, which is why every other entry is
paired), and the fixture is re-recorded. Verified by decoding every base64
value in every cassette and searching the decoded bytes for UUIDs: the
Anthropic tree is clean.

**Both listers could still spin on a cursor that repeats.** Terminating on
absence does not cover a server that echoes the same token forever — the next
request is byte-identical to the one just answered. Both now stop when the
cursor does not advance, which is what "stop the pagination loop from
spinning forever" claimed all along. Gemini gains loop-level coverage for it;
its previous tests only reached the parser.

Also: matrix row 8 named a cursor its test does not use and the surrounding
prose still described the old row set; `recorded_streamed_stop_reason` now
asserts a single terminal frame like its sibling rather than silently taking
the first; and one `assert!(a == b)` that re-parsed the cassette to build its
failure message is an `assert_eq!`.

* docs(changelog): cover the repeat-cursor guard and cursor encoding (#2334)

fix(core)!: preserve response headers on non-success HTTP errors (#2333)

* fix(core): preserve response headers on non-success HTTP errors

The transport already captured the failed response's `HeaderMap` into
`http_client::Error::InvalidStatusCodeWithDetails` (rig#2314 needed it to
read each provider's request-id header), but every normalization path then
threw the map away, so `Retry-After` on a 429 was structurally unrecoverable
by the caller — including by rig's own `RetryPolicy::retry`, which is handed
the error and cannot honor a server-supplied backoff.

`send_completion` was the clearest case: it destructured the headers-bearing
variant, read exactly one header out of it, and then either downgraded to
`InvalidStatusCodeWithMessage` (contract-less providers) or funnelled into
`ProviderResponse`, which had no headers slot (contract providers).

Capture is now preserved end to end:

- `http_client::Error::non_success_headers()` — public, because a custom
  `RetryPolicy` receives the raw transport error.
- `ProviderResponseError` gains a `headers` slot and a `with_headers` setter;
  the type is `#[non_exhaustive]` precisely so transport metadata can grow.
- Every capability error gains `provider_response_headers()`, reading from
  both the `ProviderResponse` and `HttpError` routes, and `rig-agent`'s
  `PromptError` / `StructuredOutputError` forward it.
- `with_response_headers()` attaches headers after either funnel, upgrading a
  non-success `HttpError` in place; classification and Display are unchanged.
- Capture sites: `send_completion` (transport-error and non-success-response
  paths), the SSE handshake conversion, and all three `verify()` branches.

Headers are cloned only for a failed response, so the success path pays
nothing; a 2xx error envelope therefore reports no headers, pinned by test.
`None` means "not captured" and stays distinct from an empty map.

Supersedes #2211, whose design this follows; that PR predated
`InvalidStatusCodeWithDetails` and so had to add a field to
`InvalidStatusCodeWithMessage`, making it a breaking change. Building on the
details variant makes the same capability additive.

Fixes #2210

* test(anthropic): pin header preservation against a recorded provider error

Replays the existing recorded 404 (no new recording, since the change does
not alter what rig sends) through both the unary and streaming paths and
asserts the response's own headers reach `provider_response_headers()`.

A live 429 cannot be forced cheaply or deterministically, so `Retry-After`
itself stays unit-tested against the same code path; what the recording adds
is proof that a genuine provider response — not a hand-built HeaderMap —
survives the transport, the driver's classification, and the funnel.

* fix(core): make header attachment first-capture-wins, and fix doctest paths

`with_response_headers` overwrote an existing capture on the ProviderResponse
route while leaving one alone on the HttpError route. Make both keep the
first capture — the site that saw the response is the authority — matching
how the request-id slot is stamped in sse_transport, and pin it.

The new doc examples used the `rig` facade path, which does not resolve in
rig-core's own doctests; `cargo test -p rig` does not run them, so this only
showed up under `cargo test -p rig-core --doc`.

* fix(core): preserve headers on the 2xx envelope and the sibling capability drivers

Review of the first pass found two gaps.

The 2xx error-envelope path still dropped headers, justified by not wanting
to clone the map on every successful completion. That trade-off was
unnecessary: `Response::into_parts()` hands the headers over already owned,
before the body future is awaited. Taking the response apart instead of
cloning removes the allocation *and* the carve-out, so a gateway reporting a
rate limit as `200` + `{"error":...}` + `Retry-After` — which OpenAI-compatible
providers do — now exposes it like any 429. The test that pinned the old
carve-out is replaced by one pinning the new behavior, plus one asserting the
success path still returns its payload and id.

The three sibling shared drivers (transcription, image generation, audio
generation) had the identical `status(); into_body()` shape and dropped
headers on exactly the path `send_completion` was fixed for — a custom
`HttpClientExt` that returns the non-success response rather than erroring.
Since this branch adds `provider_response_headers()` to every capability
error, leaving them unfixed would make that accessor a promise the drivers
break. All four now share one shape, each with a regression test.

Also corrects a comment in cohere/completion.rs that named the specific
transport variant its errors no longer take.

Still unfixed, and called out in the PR: the bespoke per-provider embedding
and rerank paths that bypass these shared drivers. They are unreachable on
the bundled transport, which propagates the headers-bearing transport error
already.

* docs(changelog): record the response-header preservation fix (#2333)

* docs(changelog): mark the header change breaking after #2335

`ProviderResponseError`. This branch's central design argument was that
adding a `headers` field there was additive *because* of that attribute; with
it gone, external code building the struct with a full literal must add the
field. Marked breaking and the reason stated, rather than leaving a claim the
tree no longer supports.

The `new`/`without_status` constructors and the `with_*` setters — which the
type's own docs now steer callers toward — are unaffected.

* docs(migrating): note the ProviderResponseError field and the variant switch

The 0.41 -> next section gains the mechanical fix for the one breaking part
(a full struct literal must add `headers`, or switch to the constructors) and
the behavior change that has no compile error to warn you: contract-less
non-success completions and all three `verify()` branches now surface
`InvalidStatusCodeWithDetails` instead of `InvalidStatusCodeWithMessage`, so a
`match` arm naming the old variant stops firing silently.

fix(openai): preserve the provider's response when a websocket upgrade is rejected (#2338)

A websocket upgrade the provider *rejects* never becomes a websocket. It is an
ordinary HTTP request until the provider accepts it, and this endpoint answers
a rejection exactly as its HTTP twin does. Verified against the live API with a
raw TLS handshake:

    HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
    x-request-id: req_...
    {"error":{"message":"Incorrect API key provided: …",
              "type":"invalid_request_error","code":"invalid_api_key"},"status":401}

`tungstenite` hands all three back — `Error::Http` carries the status and
headers, and its body is filled in from the read tail
(`handshake/client.rs:95-97`) — and `websocket_provider_error` was one line
that flattened the lot to `error.to_string()`. The caller got
`ProviderError("HTTP error: 401 Unauthorized")` and nothing else:
`provider_response_status()`, `provider_response_body()` and
`provider_request_id()` all `None`, so a bad key was indistinguishable from a
quota stop or a network fault.

That is the contract rig#2314 and rig#2315 established for the crate's other
two completion transports — the blocking path keeps it through
`send_completion`, the SSE connect path through `sse_transport` — and the
websocket never had it. A rejected upgrade now classifies as
`CompletionError::ProviderResponse` with the body and the id attached, reusing
the same `REQUEST_ID_HEADER` the HTTP twins read.

The rejection's headers ride along by the same rule (rig#2210, landed in
#2333 while this was in review): a `429` upgrade carries `Retry-After`, and a
caller that has to back off needs it from whichever transport refused it. This
is the same `.with_response_headers(...)` step `sse_transport` applies to its
handshake, so all three transports now answer a refusal identically.

Failures that never reached the provider have no response to preserve and stay
`ProviderError`. `Error::Http` is constructed only by handshake code, so of the
five `websocket_provider_error` call sites only the two connect ones can reach
the new branch; the mid-session sites are unaffected by construction.

Coverage is where the reachable state is. Nine unit cells in `rig-core` cover
the error space: body present/absent, request id present/absent/empty, headers
present/absent, nine status classes including the 2xx and 3xx that a non-101
response can also carry, and every non-`Http` variant except `Tls`, whose inner
error cannot be constructed portably. Two recorded cells then pin the live
shape — the first cassette coverage this transport has had, possible because a
rejected upgrade is plain HTTP. The second drives *both* transports against the
same credential in one cassette and compares the two errors, so a regression on
either side fails it.

Only the auth-class failure is recordable — the model is named in the
`response.create` message rather than the upgrade, so a bad model fails in band
on an established socket — and the matrix says so rather than leaving a silent
gap. It also records that these cells run on the nightly and merge-queue jobs
rather than the PR gate, since `websocket` is not a default feature.

fix(mistral): eight more provider bugs found by live cassette recording (#2337)

* fix(mistral): batch cap, embedding dimensions, and model-listing fields

Three more defects found by comparing the live API against what rig
models.

EmbeddingsBuilder chunked by the shared OpenAI cap of 1024 inputs per
request. Mistral's real cap is 256 -- verified live, 256 succeeds and
257 returns "Too many inputs in request, split into more batches." --
so any job over 256 documents failed outright. Mistral's own
MAX_DOCUMENTS constant said 1024 and was dead anyway: a free constant,
never a trait impl, so nothing consulted it. OpenAIEmbeddingsCompatible
now carries the cap and the generic model takes it from there.

Every Mistral embedding model reported ndims() == 0, because the
default-dimension lookup consulted OpenAI's table and Mistral has no
entry in it. A model declaring zero dimensions cannot size a vector
store. The trait gains a default_ndims hook; because the shared path
also echoes the declared width back as the request's `dimensions`
field, asking mistral-embed for its own native width is now a no-op
rather than the UnsupportedParameter error it would otherwise become.

Model listing used the shared OpenAI-shaped entry, which models neither
`description` nor `max_context_length` -- both of which Mistral sends
and `Model` has slots for. Mistral now has its own entry type.

The five model constants that no longer exist in Mistral's catalog
(pixtral-large-latest, pixtral-12b-2409, mistral-saba-latest,
open-mistral-nemo, open-codestral-mamba) are deprecated rather than
removed; each names a model that now fails with 400 Invalid model.

* fix(mistral): count audio tokens as prompt input

Mistral's audio models report prompt_tokens_details.audio_tokens
alongside prompt_tokens rather than inside it. A live Voxtral turn
answering a 375-audio-token clip reports prompt_tokens 6,
completion_tokens 2, audio_tokens 375 and total_tokens 383 -- so
mapping only prompt_tokens to input_tokens left input + output short of
the total by the whole audio payload, and rig's own usage arithmetic
did not add up on any audio turn.

PromptTokensDetails now models audio_tokens, and Usage::input_tokens()
sums the two. Non-audio turns are unaffected: the field defaults to 0.

* fix(providers): answer an n>1 stream from candidate 0, not all of them

With n > 1 the OpenAI-compatible wire interleaves chunks distinguished
only by choices[].index. The adapter took each *chunk's* first choice,
so every candidate's deltas landed in the same buffer and the caller got
an answer the model never produced -- while the blocking path answered
the same request from candidate 0 alone, so the two transports
disagreed about identical bytes.

Live proof against mistral-small-latest at temperature 1, n=2:

    index=0 delta='Z'    index=1 delta='H'
    index=1 delta='arm'  index=0 delta='ebra'
    index=1 delta='ony'

Blocking yields "Zebra"; the stream yielded the interleaving of both.

StreamingChoice now models `index` (optional -- providers streaming a
single candidate may omit it, and absent reads as candidate 0), and the
adapter selects that candidate. Single-candidate streams are byte-for-
byte unaffected, which is every existing fixture.

* fix(mistral): reconcile tool_choice with response_format, survive truncation

Two bugs from the second hunt sweep.

Mistral accepts a response format beside tools only under tool_choice
auto (or none); anything forcing a call is a 400, "`json_schema`
response type with tools is only compatible with `tool_choice: auto`".
Rig builds that combination itself: Auto output mode resolves to Native
on Mistral, so the schema rides the request, and the shared path defers
response_format until a tool result exists -- then emits it beside the
caller's standing tool_choice. Turn 1 succeeds and the tool runs; turn 2
dies, after the side effect. Finalization now relaxes the choice to auto
for exactly that turn. Relaxing the choice rather than dropping the
response format keeps the schema the caller actually asked for.

Separately, when max_tokens runs out mid-arguments Mistral still emits
the tool call, with `arguments` cut off partway through the JSON --
reproduced live at 24/32/48/64/96 token budgets, every one invalid.
Mistral's Function parsed it strictly, so the whole response failed and
the text, usage, id and finish reason went with it. The streaming path
keeps the turn and drops the unusable call; the blocking path now does
the same, leaving the Length finish reason to report the truncation.

The same strict parse exists on the shared OpenAI Function type, so
every OpenAI-compatible provider has the blocking half of this defect.
That is a wider change than this PR should carry and wants its own
cross-provider fixtures.

* docs: point this round's changelog entries at #2337

#2331 merged as the first four bugs; these eight are their own PR, so
their entries link there instead. Also reconciles with the entries main
picked up in the meantime (#2333, #2334), which sit alongside these
rather than being replaced.
